136.Name: Sonia
136.Story:
Sonja and I have known each other for years. Back then she was a wan, listless little thing, scurrying around with us in the dark, lawless alleys of the slums. She had long, flowing blonde hair - not that you'd know it under all the mud and fleas - which she still stubbornly spent ages braiding. She was one of us: another weak and downtrodden worm, mired in the silt of chaos and turmoil, all too often caught and beaten for her thievery. Now and then I would share with her some of the vegetables I'd managed to obtain and, maybe in response to such unexpected kindness, she in turn would tear off some of her stolen bread and return the favor. As the days, weeks, months dripped by, we inevitably got to know each other better.
    Oh, Sonja was a clever one. She was in and out of the various traders all year long, and knew the black market better than anyone else. Am I the slightest bit surprised that she hit it off so well with Nara? Of course not. After all, Nara was the most agile and fierce of all our dank alley thieves. Ever since they started working together, the two of them complemented each other so well that they were never again caught, instead going on to make a killing with every single job. They made sure to share their profits and goods with us, yet we still remained the target of extortion and bullying by the various other gangs.
    One evening, Sonja came looking for us. She and Nara, tired of the other gangs lording it over us, wanted to form their own group. This would give us orphans, the scurrying inhabitants of the alleys, a proper foothold in Rustport. Together with Nara, she told us of their vision, something we never would have countenanced in a million years: they wished for us to live well, able to eat and drink our fill, as one family. And so it was that the Whispers were born, and we felt we'd finally come home.

    It didn't take long for the Whispers to earn a reputation for itself in Rustport. While Nara's obvious ruthlessness and brutality terrified the other gangs, they still hadn't realized Sonja's strategy, which aimed to elevate the Whispers head and shoulders above the other Rustport gangs.
    Blood and roses... These, to me, perfectly symbolize Nara and Sonja. Nara's savagery stained the ground of this sinful land with the blood of countless opponents, while Sonja was more a gorgeous, mud-encrusted rose, tangled and bristling with the thorns of sin.
    In order to make real money, we Whispers had to carve out our own unique niche. We gradually found an emerging market in the trade of... "Special" goods, which became our best chance to make it big. Nara bribed her way to ensure the sea routes were open for the Whispers to bring back our plunder, which she held at port for Sonja to dispose of. The excellent coordination between the two have allowed us to really profit from this emerging new industry.
    As our business grew, Sonja discovered that smuggling was not without risk: while she had always respected and followed the unwritten code of smugglers, the expanding gang brought in more and more people, some of whom may not be so faithful to the criminal creed. There were those who were not above playing multiple sides for their own personal benefit. Once the smuggling lines were leaked, the Whispers had to contend not just with the threat of robbery, but also with the fact that the leaker may well be a member of our own little "family".
    Inevitably, this fear became reality. Our secret smuggling routes were leaked to rival gangs by those closest to us. Nara wiped out those who ambushed our goods, while the leaker defected to our rivals. Faced with those who had once shared bread and battle by our sides, and who now worked to harm the interests of our family, seeds of suspicion were sown and took root in the hearts of many of the Whispers.
    This caused the very first argument to erupt between Nara and Sonja. Nara wanted to publicly execute those in the Whispers who were suspected of being traitors, to serve as a warning to others. She even thought to begin with the earliest members of the gang. Her rage and distress terrified me, yet I was also cognizant of the arrogant, entitled attitude amongst many of these old "veterans". They were no longer satisfied by the wealth the Whispers generated for them, desirous of ever more power, and secretly making moves within our own ranks by leaning on the newest members.
    Sonja, however, was more hesitant to take such drastic measures. Perhaps she was reluctant to dig too deeply into the treachery of those with whom she had risen from the mud of the slums. Whatever her motive, she was unwilling to kill the traitors, preferring instead the "merciful" option of banishment.
    Their quarrel ended as Nara slammed a door and stormed off. Sonja said not a word, perhaps in resentment of her own hesitation, as she had never before had such a major disagreement with Nara. My own conjecture is that Sonja still believed in the Whispers' original purpose: to provide a stable home for the worms struggling in the mud of the slums. Now that this dream was realized, how could she evict her own "family"?

    Nara vanished. One day she set sail on an ordinary voyage, and just never returned. Sonja exhorted all Whispers to search for them, but no trace was ever found. The other gangs felt that with Nara's disappearance we had lost our most powerful deterrent, and began eyeing what had previously been unequivocally under our command. Discontent inside the Whispers also surged, and even I could hear the tavern rumors that there were plans afoot to overthrow the Whispers from within.
    Not everyone was rooting for Nara. Some of the veteran members secretly rejoiced, as they eyed Sonja's position as leader and dreamt of seizing power for themselves. For Sonja, these circumstances opened her eyes, stripping away her tolerance of and faith in the old guard. She abandoned her merciful approach, shook off the pain of Nara's disappearance, and began to ruthlessly screen all those around her. She discerns the traitors in her midst and, after a mental and physical flaying, rejects them back into the mud and slime of the slums, broken and dejected.
    No one could have seen this coming. That the girl who used to cry because her moldy bread was stolen could make such a cruel decision. Sonja retaliated against the traitors even more than Nara, until no one even dared think of betrayal, and all of Rustport was in awe. Sonja no longer showed pity to those who shared her background, while those orphans she rescued from the slums had to pay everything for the privilege.

    I almost do not recognize Sonja now. She has shaved off her long, golden hair, and carved roses into her temples. She no longer smiles at me, but beneath her ice-cold expression constantly wonders if I am tempted to betray her. She had trusted us, and we were unable to repay her with unerring loyalty. She can but watch over the Whispers and, even if she feels the task too heavy to bear alone, will never give up. She knows that only by making the Whispers even stronger, will Nara be able to find her way home.
    Sonja is an iron rose blooming among thorns. She has trodden on the corpses of countless traitors, turned her back on the last vestiges of goodwill, and climbed step by step onto the throne of power. The Whispers is not just an empire she built with Nara, but also testament to her ambition and greed.
    I am but a bystander to her life of sin, which one may call cruel, another great. She will never be satisfied with what she has and, while she used to be kind, she now wields total control over life and death in the Whispers, despite never needing to ever again dirty her own hands.

    "Desire is the rose that cuts its way through the sinful soil which is covered in blood. That is my weapon."
136.DisplayTips: Tank. Provides protection for her allies, and deals damage back at her assailants.

137.Name: OrcMaster
137.Story:
The Maulers had not yet fallen into internecine conflict when Brutus was young, and most of his rare memories of stability during childhood are from this time.
 
    Back then, the Mauler Chieftain still enjoyed a semblance of respect and authority, despite generations of depravity bringing the Maulers ever closer to ruin. Awed by his prestige, each tribe just secretly jockeyed for position and power while keeping their naked ambition concealed. The eventual death of the Mauler Chieftain, however, was like a dam bursting, releasing the pent-up aggression and bringing brutal, dog-eat-dog violence to this slice of the desert. Falkin, Centaurs, Bearfolk... All finally showed their fangs as territory, resources, and even persons all became fair game for plunder. The Maulers thus fell into decades of savage strife, the more powerful tribes massacring and annexing the weaker ones with impunity. Every day, tribes of all sizes simply vanished from this desolate, barren land.
 
    The innumerable tribes, which had once formed the mighty Maulers together, now became the architects of their own disintegration. Those without formidable military power spent every day under an oppressive cloud of dread. They hoped against hope that a mighty hero would appear and claim the throne of the Mauler Chieftain, thus ending the wearying years of bloodshed.
 
    The Blood Claw at the time, Anasta, was particularly conspicuous. In turbulent times, pure power is inextricably linked with status, and her prowess hadn't earned her the highest honor a Mauler could receive from the former Blood Claw for nothing. Anasta had the power to change the course of events in the desert, not only from her fearsome combat skills, but also because of the immense support she enjoyed from her followers. 
 
    "The Blood Claw is the most exalted among Maulers."
 
    Anasta's proclamation won her many admirers, of whom Brutus was one. He viewed Anasta as the epitome of a true warrior, and underwent harsh training to be able to join her forces. He was eventually accepted as her proud disciple, thanks to his outstanding fighting instincts and iron will. Like her other devotees, Brutus firmly believed that Anasta would inevitably be elevated to the highest station, returning the Maulers to the golden, unified age of the previous Mauler Chieftain.
 
    As expected, Anasta led her courageous and battle-hardened crew to victory after victory, claiming back the fragmented territories of the Maulers with each success. The weaker tribes, eager for protection, were the first to bend their knee, while those who opposed her relentless march were spared no mercy. The tribe chiefs were subjugated one by one, and compelled to sign treaties of alliance. Even the infamous Quicksand Claws feared the approach of Anasta's battle standard, and sought to avoid conflict.
 
    It was not all smooth sailing, however. Over the years, the balance of power amongst the tribes of the Scorched Expanse had changed. The stronger tribes were always annexing the weaker ones, while others were seeking to become more relevant by amassing troops. Pitched battles were vicious, with no side willing to admit defeat. They were so stubborn and proud that they would have a pyrrhic victory or none at all.
 
    To make things worse, in recent years a young Falkin by the name of Skriath had been making a name for himself. After the Blood Guard threw their support behind him, it was clear that this young upstart could actually pose a threat. This fear was proved well-founded as, after only a few more short years, he had firmly established himself as a serious rival to Anasta. For her part, Anasta ventured out of her camp less and less. Brutus spied her more than once lingering in her tent, head bowed over a military map, lost in contemplation.
 
    One day, Skriath himself appeared in the middle of a sandstorm, claiming he had an important matter to discuss with the Blood Claw. As an expression of his sincerity, he had with him only his personal bodyguards, led by the Blood Guard Anoki. Brutus viewed Skriath's visit as a provocation, and was about to attack in rage before Anasta waved him off. She ordered everyone else to leave, before taking Skriath alone into her tent. No one knows what passed between them, but when Skriath later went off, Anasta looked downcast, her eyes troubled.
 
    She was silent for a long time, before finally saying: "There can be only one Mauler Chieftain."
 
    From that day forth, Anasta and Skriath stood in opposition to each other. They faced each other on many occasions, but each time were evenly matched. Anasta became gradually more secluded, as if she was planning something, and occasionally unknown characters would disappear into her tent for secret discussions. All the different factions of the desert watched this cold war intently, fully aware that one of the two would become the next Chieftain.
 
    It was not long before Skriath made the first move. In the name of "Acting Chieftain," he invited all the tribe chiefs to discuss the future of the Maulers. Anasta was invited, naturally, and held her usual training with Brutus the evening before her departure. Brutus' skills had increased so quickly that Anasta had to now spar with him seriously.
 
    As the fight concluded, Anasta's voice echoed around the camp, carried on the wind.
 
    "Remember, Brutus: Warriors never stop fighting. Sometimes you will have to make some difficult choices, including those which run counter to the gaining of glory..." Anasta seemed to be half teaching Brutus, half convincing herself. "After tomorrow, the Maulers will welcome a new Chieftain."
 
    Wind-whipped sand obscured the pale moonlight, and as Brutus looked at his mentor before him, her face looked strange and unfamiliar.
 
    The next day, all the chiefs gathered, yet Anasta was conspicuous by her absence. The bolt from the blue came just as Skriath was about to call the meeting to order. Anasta, leading a band of Quicksand Claws, launched an assault on the meeting place. Heavily armed, they surrounded the chiefs and demanded each and every chief recognize Anasta as the Mauler Chieftain. None of the chiefs dared breathe out of turn, and seemed on the verge of submitting to the audacious Anasta.
 
    All at once, chaos erupted as a small squad, led by Brutus, broke through the encircling Quicksand Claws.
 
    Not long ago, Brutus had accidentally uncovered evidence in Anasta's tent of collusion with the Quicksand Claws, a secret message from the Lightbearer nobility. They had been secretly funding the Quicksand Claws, in an effort to provoke and exacerbate Mauler civil conflict. The rise of Skriath was a threat, so they decided to aid his opponent Anasta in seizing power.
 
    Brutus couldn't believe that his respected mentor could betray the warrior code and become a Lightbearer bootlicker, stooping so low as to use such base tactics to seize power. The stakes were too high, however, so he secretly assembled a small team of those he trusted most, just in case the unthinkable should come to pass.
 
    The plot was thus uncovered, and the crowd was understandably furious. If Anasta's scheme had prevailed, the Maulers would have been reduced to nothing but the Lightbearers' puppets. The chieftains, disregarding the knives held at their throats, rose as one in revolt as the totally fearless Skriath led the fight. Those encircled by the Quicksand Claws attacked from within, Brutus and his team from without, and together they forced the bandits to retreat.
 
    Anasta, seeing that the tide had turned, didn't waste any more lives on the vain fight. She, together with the remnants of the Quicksand Claws, abandoned the battle and tried to escape. Brutus gave chase by himself, adamant about getting an explanation from his mentor. All he knew, however, had been learned from Anasta. He was never able to best her before, and this time was no exception. He could only watch helplessly as this traitor, his former idol, disappeared into the desert, and demand angrily:
 
    "WHY?!"
 
    "For Mauler unity, someone must make sacrifices..."
 
    Anasta's voice came from the shadows. He could barely make her out before she took one more step forward and completely disappeared into the darkness.

138.Name: Karen
138.Story:
<css_skin_item_troopFontLargerOnly>Announcement</css_skin_item_troopFontLargerOnly>

    Heretical magic suspected at Slade Manor. Relevant bodies are investigating, but if any members of the public have information, they are urged to submit such to the Heresy Inquisition.
<css_skin_item_troopFontLargerOnly>Nora's Letter</css_skin_item_troopFontLargerOnly> 

Dear Sir/Madam,
    My dear friend, Ms. Anna Cartas, has been in the employ of Kalene Slade as a maidservant at Slade Manor for the past year. Anna is my closest confidant, and we are constantly exchanging correspondence. Yesterday, however, I received a letter saying she was in danger, but I cannot now get in touch with her!  
    I'm including her letter here, in the hope it may help the investigation. Should you find Anna, please let her know that I am awaiting her safe return.  
    NB: I believe this has to be connected with Kalene Slade.
    Warm regards.
   
<r>Nora Hill</r>
<css_skin_item_troopFontLargerOnly>Anna's Letter</css_skin_item_troopFontLargerOnly>

My Dearest Nora,
    I'm so frightfully busy these days that I've only just found time to sit and write! I trust all is well with you?
    I've been at Slade Manor for a month now, and it's exhausting learning all the ropes! I'm sure you recall I mentioned being Lady Kalene's personal maid? I'm responsible for all her daily needs and, as heir to House Slade, she's always busy managing the family's affairs. She is well-educated and erudite, speaks several languages fluently, and treats me very well. There are none of the haughty airs a noble usually has when addressing their servants. Sadly, she is very unwell and physically frail. The physician even said she might not make it to next year! Should the worst truly comes to pass, there's no telling what will happen to House Slade. 
    Madam's mental state is also deteriorating, sadly. I've seen portraits of her in the past, how magnificent and perfect she used to be. Ah well... I just want to look after her as best I can, and make her days as happy as possible.
    By the way, I heard a housekeeper say that Sir Ivan will be gracing the manor with his presence next month. Weren't he and Lady Kalene childhood sweethearts? I wonder what he's like.
    I've enclosed a little something for you as a gift! I hope you like it.  
<r>Love, Anna</r>   
 
My Dearest Nora, 
    Did you like the gift? It's good to have a nice scarf when the weather gets colder! 
    So, remember that I said Sir Ivan was coming back? Well, he's here now and just as elegant and handsome as I imagined, not to mention ever so kind. Oh, he and Lady Kalene, what a perfect match they are! If only she'd get better, maybe they could have an heir. Lady Kalene's condition has also improved since he came back, and she was even telling me how they used to go walking in the woods together. Of course, that was back when she could still walk, not like today. Ah... People who are seriously ill always seem to miss the past, and their former happiness. It's kind of like mental torture on top of physical sickness. 
    Want some juicy gossip? I'll tell you, but you have to promise me you won't tell anyone else! I bumped into Sir Ivan in the courtyard one day, and we had a little chat. He said that while he still loves his wife dearly, her illness and decline make him terribly sad. He misses the beautiful and lively wife he once had, but has steeled himself to face the inevitable. 
    Anyway, Lady Kalene always retires early these days. And it just so happens that I keep accidentally-on-purpose running into Sir Ivan. Sometimes he'll stop and talk a while, and I think sometimes I overstep the line... But I hope he doesn't mind, seeing as he keeps comparing me to the young Lady Kalene! 
    You know, sometimes I dream (even though it's clearly foolish) that maybe, one day, after Lady Kalene passes... He and I... 
    Oh, I shouldn't think such terrible things! She's been so kind to me, after all. This is just between you and me, alright? 
<r>Love, Anna</r>   
 
My Dearest Nora,
    Yet more new developments to report!
    I was cleaning my Lady's room one day, when Sir Ivan appeared and asked how things were. Nothing wrong with that, but I must have come across a right fool as I just started babbling! The issue is... Lady Kalene was awake and I swear, I'll never forget the look she gave me. She yelled at me, called me all sorts of names I didn't think a woman of her breeding would even know, and ended up coughing blood! Sir Ivan restrained her temper, but I think she has known about my previous interactions with him.
    Lady Kalene has turned cold to me. I tried to explain, but that didn't help matters, and she even looks askance at Sir Ivan now, too. For his part, he remains just as steadfastly by her side as ever. Such a kind man, a good man... Watching his wife slowly shuffling off the stage of life. Lady Kalene could have steered House Slade towards a better future with the Lightbearer Empire... But now she just sits on the bed, staring out the window. Is this the price of power by birthright alone?
    Anyway, next week another quack is coming to see Lady Kalene. This one's been recommended by a friend, but where so many famous doctors have failed, I fear this time will be no different...
    Honestly though, if Lady Kalene could recover, it would make all the difference in the world! But I can't really see such a thing happening... 
<r>Love, Anna</r>   
 
My Dearest Nora,
    Some of the manor staff have been transferred recently. It seems like every other day someone else has gone. I don't know if they've been sent to work on another estate, nor whether I would be transferred out of here one day too.
    Maybe I was wrong and he's not a quack, as ever since the doctor saw Lady Kalene, I cannot deny that her condition has improved! She can even get around without a wheelchair, and seems like a completely different person to the patient on her sickbed. What sort of medical marvel is this? 
    Sir Ivan doesn't seem overjoyed at his wife's recovery. I've seen him a number of times in the hall, coming up from the cellar with a grey, sweaty complexion... I wonder what's down there. I remember the doctor was asked to go down there for treatment...
    Lady Kalene is still frosty to me, and it seems her temperament is getting worse, too. She'll even break things on purpose, just to have me clean them up. It shames me to say it, but I almost miss the days when she seemed at death's door. At least things weren't so tense around here then. And if she fully recovers? Will everything be alright then?
    I'm going to be honest with you, my dear friend, as I can no longer ignore my feelings but must follow my heart. I think that Lady Kalene no longer loves him, and that I am a much more suitable partner for such a man.
    I have a plan. I can't tell you the details just now, but if I succeed, you'll be the first to know everything. 
<r>Love, Anna</r>  
 
Nora,
    Everything is out of control.
    They say no one can leave the manor. There's no reason given, only that it is Lady Kalene's direct order.
    Lady Kalene has completely regained her strength and beauty, and can move around freely these days. I suspect that she's aware of my intentions, but there's no turning back...
    Yes, I love him. I cannot deny it anymore. While Lady Kalene was recovering, I even had such wicked thoughts... Like what if she went back to that sick, listless husk? Why, I could... I even slipped some oleander into her wine, but she drank it down without a hiccup! It's like she's laughing at me... She knows!
    Yes, I may be guilty, but her recovery is most certainly not thanks to medical skills! It's more like some evil black magic. Her body is covered in these strange red welts, almost like some kind of marks. I think she's no longer that sick, pitied, and abandoned creature, but something else. She's changed...
    She'll never let me go... I have to get out of here, right now! But how...? 
<r>Anna</r>
 
 <css_skin_item_troopFontLargerOnly>Report into the Slade Manor Heresy Incident</css_skin_item_troopFontLargerOnly>

    Investigations into the unusual events at Slade Manor have concluded them to be connected with the spread of necromancy. The findings are as follows:
...
    Slade Manor had lost contact with the outside world for several days, most likely due to the spread of necromancy. Given that House Slade was privy to state secrets of the Lightbearers, the Temple authorized the Heresy Inquisition to enter the premises by force.
    No survivors were found inside. The deceased included Sir Ivan Slade and many domestic servants. A total of 37 victims have been identified.
...
    The cellar was determined to be the site of heretical practices. Temple investigators discovered a large number of items used in necromantic sacrifices around the area.
    The investigators failed to identify the lady of the manor, Kalene Slade, among the deceased. She had been suffering from a terminal condition since a teenager, which Lightbearer physicians had determined to be incurable. This, combined with other relevant evidence and the letters exchanged between the civilians Nora Hill and Anna Cartas, gives us reasonable grounds to suspect that Kalene Slade was colluding with Bantus. We further believe that the 37 souls lost within Slade Manor were used as a means of survival for Lady Slade, and that she has been transformed into a Graveborn.

    Kalene Slade is now considered a wanted fugitive by Lightbearers. If she is found within the Lightbearers' territory, she risks summary execution.

139.Name: SLK
139.Story: Brandishing his lethal blade, Brutus dispatched his final foe into the dust. Grasping his greatsword with both hands, he listened to the scout's account of how a group of wicked monsters had recently appeared near the Mauler border. They were said to have appeared out of thin air, attacking the surrounding villages and gradually becoming a threat to Mauler stability itself. "One more thing... That person you've been looking for was spotted in the Weatherworn Dunes." Brutus kept a neutral expression in the face of this unexpected news, but his eyes betrayed a glimmer of excitement. "Found you, Anasta." The Weatherworn Dunes lies deep within the Scorched Expanse. In this uninhabited stretch of desert, which no one rashly enters, apparently tranquil dunes conceal the lethal quicksand underneath. Yet now, on the dunes above, Brutus is locked in vicious combat, his opponent wielding a sword the height of a man. Heavy blows send sand flying as the warriors' two weapons clash again and again in the fierce desert heat. "I've been looking for you a long time, you Mauler traitor." Brutus faces none other than Anasta, his one-time mentor and former Blood Claw, she who had betrayed the Maulers before fleeing. It seems like so long ago now, when Brutus had inadvertently discovered proof of Anasta's collusion with the Lightbearer nobility, and led his followers to foil her plot to seize the position of the Wise One. Once the dust had settled, the various tribal chieftains, realizing that humans were their common enemy, unanimously selected Skriath as their Wise One. Under his leadership, the Maulers set forth upon a unified path, with Brutus as the Blood Claw. While still highly respected among the Maulers, the stain of Anasta's treachery undoubtedly still sullied the name of Blood Claw. Brutus was troubled that the name inherited from a traitor had lost its due glory. He had never fully accepted the title even within his own heart, and the historical Blood Claw cloak and crown were sealed deep within the temple and never worn. The traitor Anasta had disappeared, reviled and hated by all the Maulers. Yet throughout all the years, Brutus had never given up the hope of tracking down his one-time mentor. Now, today, he finally gazed once more upon her as she stood before him in the flesh. Even after so many years it was an oddly familiar feeling to fight with Anasta once again. While he had never before managed to best her in the past, today he was a different caliber fighter. After clashing together again and again, Brutus caught her off-balance and sent her weapon flying, before knocking her to the ground. Brutus advanced, his vicious blade pointed at Anasta's neck, yet did not strike. "You were never so ambitious and hungry for power. Why did you betray us? Why?!!" Anasta had no intention of replying, wishing only that he do what must be done to finish this battle. "TELL ME THE TRUTH!" Defeating his mentor had never been Brutus' ultimate aim. For years he had harbored suspicions about her betrayal and right now, right here, he needed to know the truth. "Then allow me to enlighten you..." Skriath's distant voice came to Brutus' ears as his figure slowly emerged from within the whirling, dancing sand, "...about what really happened." The Maulers had been divided ever since the assassination of the previous Wise One. The Lightbearers had seen an opportunity to continue destabilizing the Maulers, and secretly funded the Quicksand Claws to provoke internal conflict between the tribes. The tribal leaders, for their part, were totally unaware that their strings were being pulled. They acted just as expected, tearing each other apart while the humans reaped the benefit. Skriath and Anasta were rare visionaries among the Maulers. They astutely identified the real reason for the fracturing of Mauler society and, after contacting each other, the two kindred spirits quickly decided to cooperate with each other. The two wise Maulers fully understood that the current internal strife and divisions were preventing any hope of Mauler unification, and that intestine bellicosity would do nothing but bog down the Maulers in interminable conflict. Even if they declared unity to the outside world, this would be superficial only, as the individual tribal chieftains would never actually pledge loyalty to a unified force. These chieftains had only their own self-interest in mind and, as soon as an opportunity arose, would be sure to strike for their own gain. A common enemy was needed to truly end Mauler division and bind the tribes together in common enmity. It was evident that this common enemy had to be the Lightbearers, they who had been profiting from the internal discord of the Maulers, and that an opportunity had to be created to awaken those selfish chieftains to this reality. So the two of them acted at odds with one another, appearing to all observers as though they were contending for the leadership. In reality, however, they were secretly formulating a careful plan, and waiting for the right time to present itself. Soon enough, the Lightbearers sent word via the Quicksand Claws, promising Anasta power in exchange for eradicating the threat poised by Skriath. This was just the opportunity they had been waiting for, and decided to use supposed "treachery" to expose the Lightbearer plot. Crucial to the plan was a warrior of sufficient renown and loyalty to the Maulers, who could foil Anasta's "plot" before assuming the mantle of Blood Claw. In this way they could command their warriors to pledge allegiance to the Wise One. Brutus was just such a warrior. Brutus did not disappoint. Everything went according to plan, and the Maulers finally edged closer to unity. Anasta disappeared behind the scenes, as arranged by Skriath, until the Earth Guardian Granit was called upon by Skriath to assist in halting the spread of quicksand in the Weatherworn Dunes. Anasta was due to come too, to protect the Earth Guardian. Brutus was visibly moved by the truth, as the suspicions in his heart were at long last confirmed: This noble warrior in front of him had never truly betrayed her people. Brutus took a long, shuddering breath, while Anasta gazed upon her favored student before speaking slowly: "Sacrifices must be made, for Mauler unity... And when the tribe is in crisis, it falls to the Blood Claw to lead the way." Presently, Anasta looked to Skriath and inquired why he had come to the Weatherworn Dunes. He explained the purpose of his trip: the elemental imbalance was growing, and terrible creatures called Corruptors were rampaging, foreshadowing imminent catastrophe. Only Elemental Guardians could prevent such catastrophe but Granit was busy dealing with the quicksand and was unable to leave the desert. Crucially, some individuals were able to inherit the power of the Earth Emblem, and Skriath believed that Anasta was a prime candidate. And now Granit's voice rumbled from nearby: "There is a heavy price for accepting the Earth Emblem. The Emblem brings with it not just power, but unknown adversity. It represents a mortal attraction to all Corruptors, as the two are natural enemies and ceaselessly stalk each other. You will never know another second's true safety." Anasta did not hesitate, having long ago decided to give everything for her tribe. Just as she was about to accept her new role, Brutus strode forward. Standing in front of Granit he demanded, "Let me do this." Brutus knew that his mentor had already shouldered too much. He felt that now was the time to step up and take on her task and responsibility, no matter the price. He gazed resolutely at his mentor: "When the tribe is in crisis, it falls to the Blood Claw to lead the way." The Earth Emblem soared from Granit's body, and attached itself above Brutus' sword hilt. He is about to set foot on a new path but, before he begins, he still has one more thing to do. Brutus slowly emerges from the temple, whence he had just recovered the cloak and crown sealed within. Where once he had rejected these sacred items of the Blood Claw, now he will proudly complete his mission as the true Mauler Blood Claw. Outside the temple, a dense crowd of Corruptors had gathered, drawn by the Elemental Emblem. Faced with such a writhing mass of foes, Brutus grasps his weapon firmly and strides resolutely forward. He has eyes only for his enemy, while the sage words of his mentor echo in his heart: "Maulers, born from defiance. We possess an indomitable will that courses through our veins, and the Blood Claw is the absolute manifestation of this will. One day in the future, you shall inherit this will of ours, and become the Blood Claw. The road is fated to be difficult, surrounded by powerful enemies, outnumbered and alone. When the Tribe needs you, you must rise to the occasion. Your body a blade, carve your way forward!" Brutus' pace quickens as he rushes into the mass of Corruptors, his sharp blade felling them on all sides.

140.Name: JOA
140.Story:
The flames in the middle of the old market square had already engulfed Joan of Arc. Before losing consciousness, memories of where she had grown up flashed in front of her eyes. The destruction of that beautiful village had served as her motivation, making her determined to protect her home. In just a few short years, Joan the country girl had become Joan the country commander.
    But she would not see victory. 
    Of course, the Joan burning in agony as flames surged around her did not know of the glittering honors bestowed upon her by future generations. She had been defeated and captured a year ago, and for the past several months had been facing the most absurd accusations — a show trial with sham charges, aimed solely at sending her to the stake.
    Braced for death, Joan never expected the smoke to clear, let alone to wake up in a completely different place. Astonished, she looked around, trying to figure out what had happened. Gone was the crowded throng of peasants, the market square, and the raging flames. Instead, she looked out upon a peaceful street, lined with rows of modest houses.
    Before she had time to think if this was some kind of miracle, she was almost sent flying by a bunch of children as they ran past, laughing joyfully. A young housewife immediately poked her head out of a nearby window to apologize, while the group of children stopped to stare at this strange new arrival, shuffling and grinning awkwardly. Joan couldn't help but laugh, as she reached out to tousle the nearest child's scruffy hair.
    Her sudden, surprise relocation meant Joan, once entrusted with the weighty task of defending her country and her home, was at a total loss as to what to do. She wandered aimlessly around the small village, eventually coming across a small chapel. Hesitating only briefly, Joan entered the chapel and listened to the monks intoning their prayers.
    Would Dura, goddess of Esperia, bestow her blessings on this stranger? Joan stood in the chapel and looked at the portrait of the goddess, yet prayed not to this unknown divinity, nor felt the warmth of the Divine Light.
    The inhabitants of the tranquil little town accepted their dimensional visitor, and in the days that followed Joan lived and worked among them as if she was but a normal young woman. Joan had long since lost her sword but, while she felt the occasional pang of regret, she knew that ordinary farming tools were of more use to the peaceful residents. Sometimes, however, she would hear the familiar neigh of horses as she passed the stables, or be dazzled by the noonday sun glinting off the blacksmith's hammer. Those days, she knew that the chaos and din of battle would once again invade her dreams that evening.
    I wonder how my home is faring. Can we win? But what can I do, anyway, when I'm stuck here?
    After some time, however, Joan changed her mind.
    It was a sultry summer eve, and Joan was putting bell-mouth orchids, laid out to dry on the balcony, into baskets. She loved these beautiful flowers because they reminded her of the blue-purple irises which grew around her hometown. Suddenly, the distant sound of jingling bells from a donkey cart reached her ears.
    Joan looked around and saw several merchants rushing into the sleepy village, one of them waving his arm and shouting something about a Hypogean attack. Covered in blood and grime, they rode their donkeys without their trailing carts, having sacrificed their bulky cargo for speed. The donkeys seemed terrified too, and ignored the threats and whips of the merchants. They rushed about madly, and one of them even threw its rider to the ground.
    As Joan stared, dumbstruck, an old priest hurriedly led several of his younger brethren out from the nearby chapel. He crouched down to help the fallen merchant back on his feet while telling his brothers to help others or flee.
    Just then, the huge bell in the central square tolled. Its deep, resonant rings reverberated through the evening air. The bell called forth the villagers, the light cast by their flickering torches revealing resolute, grim countenances. One elderly man ordered his grandson to go inside, while the priest mumbled prayers for divine aid in battle. More and more young men and women assembled, clutching a variety of axes, sickles, hoes and other makeshift weaponry. While they may not have had much formal training, it was clearly not the first time they had faced a Hypogean threat.
    It would appear that this apparently peaceful village had been suffocating in the shadow of the Hypogeans.
    Joan joined the group of young villagers without a second's thought, striding with them towards the entrance of the village. She took a long, unwieldy sword from one of the villagers, its unfamiliar heft making her thankful she hadn't forgotten her fundamental training.
    Looking around her, Joan thought that the faces of the villagers looked familiar. Then she put her finger on it — the faces of her old battlefield comrades had often held the same resolute expressions. In times of peace they'd tell each other of their hometowns: the rippling fields of wheat, the lazy flocks of sheep, the jars of pickled produce. Or maybe they'd speak of snow falling softly onto pine roofs, or of grinding, crunching, creaking millstones. Then, in times of war, it would be these memories that drove them to the battlefield without hesitation.
    Joan smiled, brandishing her sword as she joined the others in rushing straight at the Hypogeans. This was her first experience of fighting such creatures, but it mattered not. None would be permitted to breach the warriors' defensive line, fighting as they were for their very homes — whether in her own hometown or in Esperia.
    
    Several days later, Joan departed for the imperial capital. The old priest had said that other dimensional visitors could be found there, and perhaps together they could find a way to fix the dimensional rifts. Joan thought of her mission: victory and freedom for her hometown and her country. But, before she could find a way home, her blade would first come to the aid of the people of Esperia.

141.Name: Alen
141.Story:
"Quickly, in there!"
    Despite the darkness and the midnight thunderstorm, Eorin saw the hollowed-out trunk of the fallen tree clearly. Heeding his mother, he nimbly squeezes inside the trunk, and waits for her to join him.
    Turning to look, he sees only her fleeing back as she runs.
    Eorin starts clambering out to chase after his mother, but just then a pair of leather boots steps into view. Eorin instinctively curls up into a ball. The stranger stops for a moment, looks around, then turns and chases after his mother. The splash of his boots in the muddy water was more terrifying to Eorin than the roar of the thunder.
    A long time later, when everything was still and silent, Eorin knew that he had lost his mother. She had hidden him there to distract the slave traders, and buy him more time to escape.
    He climbed out of the tree, wanting to find a way home, out of the dark forest. All was strange and unfamiliar, however, and Eorin found himself frozen in place, unable to move.

    "Wake up."
    The resonant voice seemed to come from far away.
    Eorin raises his head at the voice, and feels a large hand patting his shoulder before a steaming mug of tea is thrust into his hands.
    Eorin woke up properly, realizing he'd dozed off in his chair. He picked up his tea and took a sip, the warmth spreading into his belly and slightly dispelling the chill of that thundery night.
    "Thanks, Uncle Oku."
    "Come now, we've known each other over a decade! No need to be so polite." The old man sitting next to him threw some charcoal into the inn fireplace, before easily changing the subject. "You should follow Mishka's example. She's never constrained by formality!"
    Oku knew very well that Eorin had been haunted by nightmares for over ten years.

    Back then Eorin had been forced to find his way home all alone, having lost his family. He couldn't believe how anyone, in this unfamiliar land, could possibly find safe paths with only a Wilder's ability to sense nature. To survive, he ate wild fruit or pilfered what he could from the carts of passing peddlers. One day, the starving Eorin spied a carriage stopped in the middle of the path. Intending to see if there was any food to steal, he cautiously lifted the side curtain.
    A bloody scene confronted him. A Wilder, sitting cross-legged, was bandaging his own wound, two human corpses next to him. He soon noticed Eorin, and let out a low cry of surprise.
    It turned out that the Wilder man was Oku, a member of the Thorned Vengeance. This was an organization whose members had suffered at the hands of outsiders, so they came together to wreak vengeance upon them. For Oku, his daughter had been kidnapped by humans, and he had spent all the years since in a mad search for her. On this occasion, he had been hot on the heels of these two human merchants, who had sneaked into the Dark Forest to steal rare herbs. He'd followed the trail of the merchants almost to the Lightbearer Empire when he met Eorin.
    Eorin tagged along with Oku as he headed home, suffering nightmares almost every single night. When he learned that his parents had been kidnapped, Oku readily agreed to help him search for them, and would gently coax him to sleep. He'd look at Eorin's little face, brows still tightly furrowed, before thinking of his daughter and trying to push the ominous thoughts from his mind.
    Eorin and Oku talked after getting back to the Dark Forest, as he wondered if it might be better to send him to a Vulpen village. Eorin, however, wanted to stay with Oku.
    "I want what you do. To get my revenge on those people." Eorin looked at Oku, his crimson eyes flashing with fire.
    Oku felt a little awkward, and wondered if maybe Eorin had gotten the wrong idea when he saw the two humans he had killed. Eorin was still a child, after all, and children should not be involved in war.
    Hearing Oku's explanation, Eorin retorted, emphasizing every word: "I am already involved."
    Ultimately, Oku sighed and relented, accepting Eorin as the youngest member of the Thorned Vengeance.

    After joining the Thorned Vengeance, Eorin was keen to learn combat skills from his elders, and asked the scholars of the group—who were studying humans to more effectively fight the enemy—to help trace his parents. It was only then that Eorin learned what happened to his parents.
    Like the other Wilders, Vulpen were imbued with forest blood by Dura, allowing them to sense and perceive all of Nature. For the rapacious humans, this meant using Vulpen to discover treasures hidden in the earth.
    This was the reason that Eorin and his parents were taken. The plan was to traffick them to some desert mines in the Lightbearer Empire, to live out the rest of their brief, miserable lives in the raging sandstorms. The number of Wilders in the mine had to be replaced every few years, as accidental deaths were all too common. The change in climate damaged their skin, while the fine dust and particulate matter clogged their lungs, not to mention the various strange vapors which arose from the alchemists' crucibles. But as far as the mine owners were concerned, what were a few insignificant Wilders, when there was so much precious amber to excavate?
    Eorin fell silent upon finding out the truth. He built a small hut near a marsh, deep in the forest, and spent every waking moment honing his fighting skills with diligence and intensity that worried Oku.
    It wasn't long before Eorin ventured even deeper into the forest in search of the toughest wood he could find. He asked a local craftsman to fashion a detachable spear, then attempted to cultivate some wonderful swamp spore on the blade and hilt. At first, no one could work out what exactly Eorin was up to. Several years later, however, on his first mission for the Thorned Vengeance, an enemy's wound erupted in a sparkle of strange fireworks. From then on, everyone knew that Eorin had perfected a fighting style all of his own.
    It didn't take many years for the thin, weak boy to grow into a tall, strong young man. After several twists and turns, Eorin finally tracked down the slave trader who had trafficked his family. Eorin tortured his captive into unconsciousness with a toxic fungus, before coolly noting down everything he had revealed under duress. Finally, he delivered the final blow with a chilling calm.
    After the mission was over, his Thorned Vengeance companion couldn't help but tell the others that it was like seeing a demon with a face like ice. When the news reached Oku, it reminded him of something seemingly inconsequential that had happened in the past. One day, the first time that Eorin met Mishka, the young girl of the Bearfolk whom he had taken in, he immediately produced a beautiful silver coprinus flower from spores to amuse her.
    Eorin was unaware of all of this gossip. The information extracted from the slave trader provided the location of his true enemy, so off he went, headed for the Lightbearer Empire. This time, Oku accompanied him.
    Now, Eorin and Oku have arrived at this small Lightbearer town. Once again, the incident from ten years ago invaded his dreams, but this time Eorin believes the nightmare will soon be over.

    Several days later, the owner of a famous mine in the Lightbearer Empire died suddenly from some strange disease. It was said that the doctors who had rushed to see him—but were only in time to see his corpse—were shocked at the strange, thick algae which blanketed his lungs.

142.Name: Patronus
142.Story:
One stormy afternoon not long ago, when I'd finally managed to get the supplies to that border camp before it was totally dark, I encountered an emaciated, scruffy old man. He was squatting, clothes ragged and eyes hollow, under the dilapidated roof of a ruined house opposite the camp. In this place, so close to the front lines, it was not uncommon to see refugees whose homes had been destroyed in the conflict, but I felt there was something different in the eyes of this fellow.
 
    When the rain eventually stopped, I was able to make my escape from the anxious grumbling of the soldiers in the camp. I was cheering my expected peace and quiet too early, however, as the old man was already on his feet and speaking as if through tears: "Alas! O, alas, he is coming! Tarnos, the radiant fang! The watchdog of the gods, with a heart of stone! His eternal atonement begins once more..."
 
    I was startled to say the least, even more so when the old man suddenly grabbed my collar in a vice-like grip: "All because Tarnos' radiance has been stained by that which he guards, only by the blood of every single Hypogean who escaped into this world can his sins be cleansed."
 
    In my frantic attempts to break free from the old man's grasp, I slipped and fell to the ground. Just as I was about to get back up, I was distracted by a commotion from within the camp. First I heard the shouts of the soldiers, followed by the sound of pots shattering and barrels breaking. Then came the blood-curdling screams and wails of horror, before the very last thing I hoped to ever hear reached my ears: the roar of Hypogeans.
 
    Flames were already licking the back of the wooden barricade, and I knew this place was soon to become a living hell. I tried to grab the old man's arm, thinking I could save at least one life, but he covered his head and began to shake uncontrollably. Sobbing, his tears soaking the back of my hand, he cried: "He has come! He is here! I can feel it! The brand on my body burns anew... He who cursed me approaches... Is today the day he takes me away?"
 
    BANG! With a loud crash, the gates of the camp were ripped apart as easily as paper, and a Hypogean appeared, holding half a set of armor. It look towards us before scratching its head, and I knew I was finished. The old man wailed even louder before dropping to his knees and flinging his arms open, as if welcoming the Hypogean. For its part, the Hypogean approached him slowly, with great interest, as if happy for and accepting of this human's servile reception. I could already smell the foul stench emanating from it, but my legs were so weak I could do nothing but lean against the tree behind me.
 
    Just as I closed my eyes and thought of my dear, departed mother, there came a heavy thud, followed by a jet of sticky, stinking liquid right in my face. I somehow overcame the ringing in my ears to open my eyes, and saw that a bizarre pillar had fallen from the sky and squished the Hypogean into a quivering, fleshy mess. I rubbed my eyes but they had not deceived me: this ornately carved pillar, majestic and solemn, was clearly not of this world.
 
    The old man was shouting at the pillar, his expression intensely strained. As the ringing in my ears slowly subsided, I could make out what he was yelling: "No! NO! Curse you, Tarnos! You were meant to come after me, not that Hypogean! I cannot be your revenge bait forever! I have already fled to this desolate place, where next will you drive me?!"
 
    I followed the old man's gaze and saw a figure in the shadow of the pillar. Beneath flowing white hair were golden veins which circulated across the black, statue-like body, while both legs were sunk deeply into the hard rock. More pillars came screaming down out from the sky, and the grotesque cracking and thudding sounds of the other Hypogeans being crushed continued to emanate from the camp.
 
    The old man screamed profanity at the figure: "Curse you! I curse you, Tarnos! 'Twas you who prevented Dura from giving fire to humans, prevented us from gaining power! You see us only as insects, crawling around the shackles of your mission! Thus the people have detested and feared you from the first day they came to know you! They reject you! Forget you!"
 
    The old man's yells changed into a tone of malicious taunting: "While you may be able to sever humans' communication with the gods, you can never prevent the Hypogeans from calling to us! Their power will allow us mere mortals, whom you ignore, to shake the very mountains! You, however, will never find redemption, hahaha!"
 
    "Petty ambition is the reason your people secretly court the Hypogeans? This thirst for power that is not yours?" Tarnos finally replied to the old man, though I could not see his face.
 
    The old man was clearly irritated: "Haha... Petty ambition? Tell me, wherefore the gods enjoy eternal life, holding themselves far above the masses, while we humans must but simply accept our mortal fate? Why is it our lot to be born weak and powerless? Where do we err in wishing for power commensurate with our intelligence?"
 
    "Human wisdom and emotion far surpass those of other creatures, yet these eventually become breeding grounds for greed." Tarnos' voice was chilling, "Dura entrusted me with watching the Barred Gate, yet those followers of the Hypogeans maintain their foolish obsession, as they try in vain to break the seal and loose the Hypogeans back into Esperia. This is a blasphemy I will never allow."
 
    "Ahahaha!" The old man's demented laughter became even more crazed. "Yes, you vilified us. Persecuted us. Exiled us. But did we not succeed in the end? Those insufferably arrogant gods were dealt a crushing blow, while we were rewarded with the power of the Hypogeans!"
 
    "That was my failure. I will not deny it." Tarnos' ice-cold eyes flashed from the shadows.
 
    "Ahaha! So, look at you now, you stubborn, cruel watchdog! To punish yourself, you go so far as to encase your legs in stone, vowing to never again take a single step until all Hypogeans have been exterminated. Do you really think this is sufficient to expunge the shame of your desertion? How ridiculous!" The old man's tone became embittered and hateful once again, "But if your goal is the eradication of all Hypogeans, why do you yet brand us and endlessly drive us away?"
 
    "The price of power for Hypogean worshippers is to become the vanguard of their evil, so you likewise become my perfect bait." Tarnos thus replied.
 
    "What sort of god are you? These are the actions of demons!" The old man buried his face in his hands and appeared to weep. The rain had started again, soaking his disheveled hair, while the strange golden brand on his forehead appeared to emit a faint glow.
 
    So immersed was I in the dreadful scene that I almost forgot I was present. But suddenly the old man leapt at me with unnatural agility, a demonic weapon fragment clutched tightly in his hand and aimed straight at my chest. I had not even time to shout before Tarnos was in front of me, grabbing the old man tightly and hoisting him into the air.
 
    "Kill... Me..." The old man managed to utter these two words, before vainly stabbing at Tarnos' arm with his weapon, almost as if in supplication.
 
    "I will not let you escape so easily." Tarnos snapped the old man's weapon as if it were a twig, then threw him to the floor. "Go. Bear my brand. The fate of you feral curs will ever be thus, even unto my redemption comes to pass."
 
    "Never. That is impossible! Hahaha, Tarnos, you avowed guardian, never will you see the day that your sins are fully repaid!" The old man frantically fled from our sight, scrabbling and stumbling into the depths of the wasteland.
 
    I do not know when it was that Tarnos departed. All I know is that when the rain stopped, all traces of what had just transpired had been washed away, as if it had never happened. Yet the actions of that merciless deity conjured nightmares within me, his name deeply engraved in my psyche: Tarnos, he whose Hypogean hunt will continue till the end of days. There will be no mercy, no quarter, no respite.
