143.Name: WNT
143.Story:
Solise never thought about leaving the Dark Forest. When young, she often listened to the elders speak of myriad dangers which lay outside, warning her to never leave the forest lest she put herself in peril. Fortunately, the Dark Forest was sufficiently large to accommodate all of Solise's passion—botany. Truly, there was no better paradise for an ardent botanist than the Dark Forest. Moreover, Solise was a Flower whisperer, a talent which granted her the ability to communicate with plants, and call upon Floral Specters.
 
    She would wander through the forest, always in her dark green cloak, listening to the whispers of the trees on the breeze, or the murmur of the flowers in the dew. The whole Dark Forest was like her own private garden.
 
    At some point in time the trees began to wither, and the forest's whispers turned into moans, filling Solise's ears with the sounds of suffering. Unable to ignore the anguish of the forest, she attempted to heal the plants with a remedy of her own making, but to no avail. Eventually, a Floral Specter told her of the magical power to be found at Yuexi Spring, a power able to relieve the plants' suffering. Despite the path to the spring being long and dangerous, Solise was determined to save the jungle, and decided to risk the journey.
 
    Fate shows no favor to those who take their first steps on the path of adventure, and danger can strike quickly. On the way to Yuexi Spring, Solise was surrounded by a group of unfamiliar monsters. Lacking combat skills, her maiden adventure almost came to an early conclusion. Solise panicked, but suddenly a young man named Eorin appeared and rescued her by beating back the monsters. The effort exhausted her savior, however, and he fell unconscious. Solise brought him back to her little herbalist hut, and treated his wounds with her homemade remedies.
 
    Eorin told Solise that those monsters were called Corruptors, and were born of the elemental imbalance that even now was eroding the entire forest. He had come to the Dark Forest in the hope of finding a way to stop this calamity. The pair then decided to travel together to Yuexi Spring, once Eorin had sufficiently recovered.
 
    During his convalescence, Eorin told Solise much about himself and his past: from good childhood memories with his family, through to all the wonderful things he had seen while traveling over the years. Solise was particularly fascinated by his stories of the outside world, and marveled at the breadth of his knowledge. At the same time, however, she occasionally glimpsed the pain he concealed in his eyes, perhaps caused by his experiences in the outside world—experiences she had never had. For the first time, the thought of leaving the forest entered Solise's mind.
 
    "Solise, there comes a day when every seedling breaks through the soil. When the current crisis facing the forest has passed, we can explore the world outside together."
 
    After many days' recuperation, Eorin's wounds were finally healed, and the two of them set off for Yuexi Spring. In torrential rainstorms, Eorin led Solise through all the challenges the forest presented. The two acted in concert to successfully escape the dangerous Corruptor Caves, while evening in the Dreamwood saw the pair float through fantastical scenes as if in a dream... Finally, after overcoming many hardships, they arrived at Yuexi Spring.
 
    Beneath the spring a mysterious symbol glowed, the Water Emblem. It was the existence of this emblem which imbued the spring water with the strength to resist the erosion. Solise collected some of the water to study for medicinal purposes, and then called Eorin to leave. He did not respond, but instead gazed intently at the Water Emblem, a strange look flashing in his eyes.
 
    "The Water Emblem is right here... Such power should be wielded by the Thorned Vengeance."
 
    Eorin was a member of the Thorned Vengeance, and finding the Water Emblem was his real purpose. The Thorned Vengeance had long disapproved of the Green Creek Council, deeming the Oak Sages outdated and pedantic, never daring to use the might of the Wilders, whether the Elemental Altar or Emblems, as weapons. Only by placing power in the hands of the Thorned Vengeance, could the forest be truly protected. Thereafter they could emerge from the forest to punish those who had dared encroach, and even incorporate other factions into the fold of the Wilders. Stubborn, passive tolerance could only result in Wilders being bullied and harmed by other forces, as had happened to Eorin's own family—his happy, carefree childhood had long since been destroyed by invading outsiders.
 
    "Go outside the forest and see, Solise! See how your Wilder brethren are so bullied and humiliated by others!"
    "You are like the ostriches of the Scorched Expanse, thinking that by burying your head in the sand you can ignore all danger. No matter how tough a weed is, it can never escape its destiny of being trampled underfoot. Only by facing the invaders with thorns can they be made to feel fear, and the Water Emblem will become the thorns in our hands."
 
    Solise tried to dissuade him, as she had learned from the Floral Specter that, should the Elemental Emblem be taken, then the spring would lose its ability to withstand the encroaching erosion. Her pleas fell on deaf ears, however, as Eorin trapped her in place before diving into the spring in an attempt to seize the Emblem. But it was like a mirage, and no matter what Eorin tried, he was unable to touch it. He sat dejectedly on the shore, the power to control his fate so close, yet as far away as the moon, and fell into unprecedented despair.
 
    "Eorin, the Elemental Emblems should never be a source of conflict."
 
    Solise was about to say more when a sudden commotion arose from within the forest. Eorin's actions had revealed the Elemental Emblem's power to the Corruptors, countless numbers of which had flooded forth and surrounded them. Eorin set free Solise, then pushed her outside the encircling Corruptors with a bitter smile. The two were separated by the flood of Corruptors, but Solise's familiarity with the forest enabled her to evade her pursuers. She could have fled to safety, but stopped running when she heard the frenzied howls of Corruptors in the distance.
 
    She rushed back to Yuexi Spring, using Floral Disruption to confound the Corruptors along the way. She finally found Eorin, despairing and awaiting death, but Corruptors stood between them. They surrounded Eorin, and began to move slowly towards the Elemental Emblem. If they succeeded in acquiring it, then all hope of saving the forest would be lost. Solise seemed to hear the forest's final cry for help. Unable to sit idly by and watch her garden wither in agony, she clutched her remaining potions and prepared to rush into the crowd of Corruptors.
 
    Perhaps the Water Emblem sensed the threat posed by the Corruptors, or maybe it was in response to Solise's determination to protect the forest, sudden brilliance burst forth from Yuexi Spring. The Emblem had revealed its true form. With a sprinkling of her potion, Solise dived into the spring, her figure overlapping with the Emblem.
 
    "The Emblem is the power to protect.
    "Born to shield living beings from elemental imbalance.
    "Elemental chaos is spreading.
    "Restless shades make the forest mourn.
    "Countless creatures writhe in pain.
    "O torrents, hear my prayer.
    "Lend me your strength.
    "Protect all this ear can hear!"
 
    Crystal-clear water surged skywards, while the figure of Solise coalesced with the spring itself. She waved a staff formed from the Emblem, turning the water in the air to rain, which fell upon every inch of Yuexi Spring. Soaked by the sudden showers, the Corruptors retreated one by one, while the trees and plants seemed to stretch out in the fresh rainfall. Solise knew, however, that the crisis confronting the forest was far from over. She would have to leave her garden, leave her forest, and find a way to stop the calamity for good.
143.DisplayTips: Support. Fights alongside the water spirits she summons, offers powerful healing to allied heroes, and converts overhealed health into buffs for allied heroes or more damage to enemies.

144.Name: GOR
144.Story:
You won't find a swordsman finer than a witcher. Take Geralt of Rivia, the famous monster slayer. Fearless and deadly in battle, he owes his exceptional dexterity to rigorous training and a mutagenic process called the Trial of Grasses. As a boy, Geralt was put in the care of Vesemir, a witcher from the School of the Wolf. His instruction complete, Geralt left the witchers' stronghold, Kaer Morhen, to travel the world and make his living by hunting down bloodthirsty monsters. He carries two swords, the silver one for beasts and the steel one… For humans, apparently. At least that's what the common folk say.
    Though posing to be devoid of all emotion and trying to remain neutral no matter the circumstances, Geralt can't help but feel things and take sides all the time. His love for Yennefer was celebrated in many a song and he would literally take on the whole world to save his adoptive daughter, Ciri, from anyone who'd dare lay a hand on her. Protecting Cirilla got Geralt involuntarily entangled in the affairs of kings and sorcerers.
    When it seemed that Yennefer and Geralt would finally have their 'happily ever after', the sorceress was kidnapped by the Wild Hunt, a spectral army travelling across worlds. Geralt offered himself to the Hunt in exchange for Yennefer and rode with the Hunt for a while before being freed by Ciri. Destiny once again embroiled him in political affairs of the world, but eventually made his and Yennefer's paths cross again.
    On one of their new adventures, something went wrong with Yennefer's teleportation spell and the two ended up in the world of Esperia. Geralt, whose hate of portals only ever deepened, now has to look for allies who could help him and Yennefer find a way to return to their world…
144.DisplayTips: Warrior. Uses the Witcher Signs with his sword skills to attack enemies continuously and disrupt them, and magic potions to buff his abilities.

145.Name: YNF
145.Story:
Always accompanied by the scent of lilac and gooseberries and dressed in black and white, Yennefer of Vengerberg is famous for her beauty and power. The raven-haired sorceress has made a name for herself as one of the most skilled and ambitious mages of her time. Member of the Supreme Council of Sorcerers and advisor to kings, yet always walking a path of her own choosing, Yennefer played an important role in the fate of the Northern Kingdoms. 
 
    She first met Geralt of Rivia in the town of Rinde where the two had a run-in with a mighty Djinn. On that fateful day their destinies intertwined forever after the Djinn granted Geralt's last wish. Several years later, Yennefer took upon herself to teach the witcher's adoptive daughter, princess Cirilla of Cintra, the basics of the art of magic and started to treat the girl as her own. She used all her powers to protect Ciri from those who wanted to hurt her. 
 
    When it seemed that Yennefer and Geralt would finally have their 'happily ever after', the sorceress was kidnapped by the Wild Hunt, a spectral army travelling across worlds, who wanted to use her as bait to capture Ciri. Geralt offered himself to the Hunt in exchange for Yennefer. Having recovered from her imprisonment, the sorceress struck a deal to find Ciri with Emhyr van Emreis, the Emperor of Nilfgaard. Destiny reunited her with Geralt once again and the couple set out to search for their daughter together. 
 
    On one of their new adventures, something went wrong with Yennefer's teleportation spell and the two ended up in the world of Esperia. Now Yennefer must find a way to fix the spell so that she and Geralt can return to their own world…
145.DisplayTips: Mage. A sorceress that attacks with Frost and Thunder Magic. Her Barriers provide buffs for all allied heroes.

146.Name: Chimera
146.Story: Chapter 1 The slave Canisa reclined in the cell. While she couldn't say that her current life in prison was unbearable, dark doubts did still linger and distract: What exactly was her purchaser, a human mage, up to? Everyone was locked up here with nothing to do every day but be examined, with all physical changes carefully recorded. Canisa stretched languidly, her gaze flickering across the other slaves. She'd only been here a few days, and was only now more or less familiar with the others. She spotted the figure of Ruke lurking amidst the shadows, only to find him looking right back at her. She couldn't help but glare at him, but he just smiled contemptuously and rattled his chains by shaking his glorious mane, of which he was so proud. Despite everyone being equal prisoners here, Canisa still clearly recalled the atrocities committed by the Leonine against the Satyrs. The two clans lived at opposite ends of a tributary in Dura's Gift, and bore long-standing historical enmity. Many of Canisa's kin had perished in battle against the Leonine and, after their clan's defeat, many of those who had been taken prisoner became slaves. So it was that Canisa had been passed through the hands of many slave traders, only to end up here. She'd never expected to see Ruke here and, from his appearance at least, life was not so easy for the Leonine now. Canisa held her head high in reply, but just then happened to catch sight of the skylight embedded in the ceiling. The sun had just set, and while the sky was still ablaze with the afterglow, the Burning Plume of Obsiornis at the zenith was particularly dazzling. Canisa woke with a start in the middle of the night. The full moon shone brightly, making it easy for her to spot Ruke's furtive actions. Ha! No wonder he'd skulked in the shadows all day, preventing anyone from getting too close—it appeared there was a small hole in the wall! "Ahem..." Canisa cleared her throat quietly. A nearby bearfolk, lost in slumber, made an incoherent noise and rolled over irritably. Ruke paused, his head turning immediately towards the door of the prison. When no guards were seen, he looked around and was faced with Canisa's sly smirk. The next day, Ruke intentionally picked a fight with a nearby centaur, who eventually moved off indignantly to the opposite corner. Seeing this, Canisa immediately stood up and began to sneeringly mock Ruke, while arrogantly gathering her chains and moving across to sit beside him. The whole while, her face bore an expression which seemed to say, "And what are you going to do about it?" That evening, Ruke continued to subtly pry bricks from the wall using a link of his chain. He would remove each one before placing it gently back in the hole. In this way, although the hole in the wall appeared only the size of a single brick, in reality, a sizable area had been loosened. "Tch. Tomorrow, all I have to do is give it a good shove and I'll be out first. But you, big oaf, will definitely get wedged in there and die." Canisa spoke softly, watching in satisfaction as Ruke's expression darkened, while her hand continued to toy with the loose bricks. The third day, the corpse of a Jackalman was placed in front of their cell door. It transpired that he had been one of the prisoners in another cell who had caused a little trouble and taken advantage of the commotion to attack the guards. Alas, he had not considered that the heavy iron bars could have been enchanted with a terrible curse, which led to a horrible and agonizing demise. The human mage who had collected them all here placed the Jackalman's body at the door of each cell, as a reminder to behave. The whole prison was abuzz with the news and, according to a Falkin, this Jackalman had been betrayed by another prisoner, apparently as part of some feud between their clans. When she heard this, Canisa couldn't help but glance over at Ruke, and the two of them eyed each other suspiciously. Just then, a snake which had slithered in between the bars and wrapped itself around a Centaur's hind hoof was violently shaken off. Everyone else was distracted by this, and they grabbed torches to drive the snake off. Canisa, however, looked away and remained silent. When night fell, the two of them began shifting the bricks once more. Neither of them said a word. Canisa estimated that, barring any accident, it would take another three days for Ruke to be able to break through the wall. After that, she would no longer have to spare a thought about her Leonine enemy. Chapter 2 An accident, however, was soon to occur. There was something very wrong with the food today. It was like some grubs or worms had found their way into it—and thence into the body of whoever ate it. Canisa shivered and shook her head, hoping it was just her imagination. But it didn't take long before she was wracked with a jolt of searing agony, and she felt as if all her innards cramped at once, her organs all twisting and constricting around each other. Looking around at the other prisoners, she saw their faces contorted and pained too. Was it possible they were afflicted with the same sickness? As she collapsed to the ground, Canisa gazed up at the skylight in despair, the Finch Tail constellation blurring and fading in her vision. "C'mon, hold it together." A gentle, supportive voice spoke in her ear. As Canisa slowly swam back to consciousness, she saw that the speaker was unexpectedly none other than the human mage. Shocked, she could not even muster a response, but only look around at the several torch-bearing doctors who stood nearby and surrounded the human mage, and they all seemed poised and waiting for something to happen. "The filth in your veins will soon be cleansed, and the Ya will recover their pure humanity. Be patient just a little longer; we are on the verge of ushering in a new era of peace." His tone may have been gentle and kind, but Canisa felt as though she'd just been sucker punched. She finally understood the reason behind the constant physical monitoring. Suddenly, a furious roar came from the prison. It was Ruke! No, not just Ruke. The Falkin, Bearfolk, and Centaurs were roaring too... And Canisa. A guttural, despairing wail came from the throats of every prisoner as they endured the seething pain that boiled within. They struggled to reach the human mage or even bite him, but were too exhausted. None could get close to him, let alone inflict a wound. He only looked upon them arrogantly, his expression expectant. A final surge of regret hit Canisa, as she lamented how generations of internal Mauler conflict had caused them all to forget their greatest foe. Had they but one more ally, they would have escaped long ago. But as it was, she and Ruke did not trust the Bearfolk, nor the Centaurs, and thus they were now reaping the consequences of this distrust. The snake undulated easily in between the iron bars. It looked at the fallen prisoners, lying in pools of blood, and closed its eyes. It inhaled long and deeply, seeming to relish the iron tang of blood in the air. "What a rich, delicious aroma! So many humans... Such intense hatred." "No! Not human!" Canisa screamed in silence to herself. It was too humiliating, a Mauler warrior perishing not on the battlefield, but in a ridiculous experiment arrogantly designed to turn Maulers into humans! It chuckled cruelly, as if taunting Canisa: "But your body has really changed... I wonder, if you're truly human now?" No! No! Not human! "No? Very well then... If you surrender yourselves to me." Chapter 3 Canisa felt a little strange when she finally woke up. She turned her head and saw a wing erupting from her arm, a wing eerily reminiscent of those of the Falkin... She did a double take, as it didn't appear to even be her arm. As for her leg... And, uh, what about her tail? The snake rippled into sight from behind her, flicking its forked tongue at her. Canisa couldn't help but laugh; was this her new body? Her Mauler brethren were with her now, she could feel herself brimming with their strength! Never again would she dread the frail human form... "Hey, your horn poked me." Canisa looked to the other side and came face to face with Ruke. They looked into each other's eyes. Ha! Just as well. The Maulers could never really have been joined any other way. She and Ruke would have a good long time together. Long enough to argue their fill, and settle old scores. The next moment, Canisa was laughing as she smashed the chains with her giant Bearfolk paw, while Ruke snatched the mage's torch with his teeth and began setting the whole prison systematically alight. "Who would want to become human?! Arrogant idiot!"
146.DisplayTips: Tank. A Hypogean that can pass on some of the direct damage they receive to enemies, and summon a Cage of Fire to weaken and control enemies trapped within it.

147.Name: Flora
147.Story:
Nevanthi wandered the length and breadth of Hathor before she came to the Island of the Banished. As the Wood Guardian of Esperia, when she finally emerged from her forest into the wider world, she was insatiably curious about human society.
 
    Dressed as a traveler, she had entered a city and, by virtue of her botanical knowledge, happened to fall in with a noblewoman who had a passion for flora. It wasn't long before the noblewoman invited Nevanthi to come to visit her garden.
 
    Greenery of all descriptions filled the garden. It also boasted perfectly-trimmed topiary, the plants of which looked a far cry from their natural appearance in the wild. Glass enclosed the whole garden which, according to the noblewoman, could maintain a constant temperature; more importantly, it also kept the lowly weeds from gaining a foothold.
 
    However, no matter the number of rare or valuable plants, Nevanthi could not muster any enthusiasm for the garden. These plants were perfectly adapted to their natural homes high up on cliffs, or deep in wooded valleys. But now here they were, having been forcefully dug up and transplanted into this crowded garden.
 
    When Nevanthi admitted how she felt, the noblewoman's reaction was beyond anything she could have foreseen. The noblewoman had hoped that Nevanthi would stay with her forever, living in her mansion and taking care of the garden. When she realized that Nevanthi was not to be persuaded, she summoned the guards to forcibly detain her.
 
    Nevanthi thus called to the plants in the garden, summoning vines and tendrils to erupt from the earth. She turned to leave, abandoning the noblewoman and her guards as they were immobilized by the hostile flora.
 
    The more Nevanthi experienced human settlements and cities, the more her dislike of humans grew. They always tried to take the things they liked for themselves, yet were never satisfied, as if there was a hole in their soul that could never be filled. Moreover, the human heart was akin to a dense forest, impossible to know whether verdant springs or foul sludge lay concealed within. This realization drove her to steer clear of humans, and she took to wandering from place to place, admiring the intrinsic, simple beauty of flowers and trees in nature.
 
    As she crisscrossed the whole continent, Nevanthi decided to aim for the ocean. Thus did she turn her meandering steps towards the remote Island of the Banished, a desolate, barren place.
 
    This island is home to a group known as the Tainted. Former innocent citizens of Bantus, they were slaughtered and forcibly transformed into Graveborn under the Thoran, the Fallen King. After escaping the tyranny of Bantus, they fled to the remote Island of the Banished, there to take refuge in rejection of the rest of the world.
 
    The world, for its part, views them as a group of unfortunate from whom fate has taken almost everything. And yet, they don't just survive, but live. They are not just putting on a brave smile in the face of adversity, but have genuinely found contentment in living in the moment. They are grateful for their small island, far removed from the strife and conflict of the world. If you haven't seen it for yourself, it's hard to even imagine so much laughter and life in a place populated by the dead.
 
    Nevanthi saw life at its most beautiful in these "unfortunate" people, tough but exquisite flowers blooming among the rubble. 
 
    Nevanthi gradually grew to know them well. She would occasionally help with things like house repairs, for when a creeper climbs an old wall, the whole structure becomes more stable. One among the Tainted caught Nevanthi's eye in particular: the youth Kerr. A Graveborn child, an almost cruel concept which indicates a life lost far too soon. Kerr was the only child on the island, whither he had fled with his parents after being forced to become Graveborn at the tender age of eight.
 
    Nevanthi noticed that Kerr would also furtively look at her, as if he wished to say something. After some gentle questioning, Kerr shyly began to speak, revealing that he wished Nevanthi to teach him how to look after a young tree. As Graveborn, Kerr would never grow up, so he planted a sapling to grow bigger and taller in his place. Every time he saw that it had grown a little, it was almost as if he had too. Recently, however, his sapling seemed to be sick, as it was growing no longer.
 
    Under Nevanthi's guidance and Kerr's diligent care, the sapling gradually recovered. Then they made a promise: to watch the sapling grow into the tallest tree on the entire island. Kerr beamed with confidence and delight, but then his expression became pained and he suddenly collapsed to the ground.
 
    Nevanthi hurriedly took Kerr back to his parents, who told her that this was a Graveborn curse, and the price all Tainted paid for their escape from Bantus. For every now and then, the Tainted would be wracked by searing, soul-deep agony. Adults could will themselves through the pain, but Kerr was just a child.
 
    Seeing Kerr's features, distorted in suffering, Nevanthi stretched out her hands. The very breath of life flowed from her and enveloped Kerr, who gradually became calm.
 
    Nevanthi was filled with misgiving as she left Kerr's house. She wondered if the Tainted would turn out like humans after all, and want her to stay on the Island of the Banished to ease the suffering of all. This was not something she wished to see, and knew that if the time came, she would have to leave the island.
 
    But when she opened her door the following day, all her worries vanished like smoke in the wind. Kerr stood just outside, tightly clutching a small bag. Inside were all the seeds of the island that the Tainted had managed to gather. Although Nevanthi could ease their pain, the Tainted did not take her help for granted, as they knew all too well what it was like to be bound. They harbored no demands, and merely offered their heartfelt gratitude for her help.
 
    "Are you going to leave, Nevanthi?"
    "How could I leave? The sapling isn't yet fully grown, silly."
147.DisplayTips: Support. Greatly boosts the survivability of her allies and highly compatible with allies who are able to summon entities.

148.Name: SBD
148.Story:
Baden evaded the swarms of Corruptors to make it to the very heart of the Island of the Banished. There, deep in the forest, vines twisted and knotted together to form a cage, in which a sleeping beauty could be glimpsed. Seeing that she was uninjured, Baden gave a sigh of relief before quietly calling her name. 
 
    "Nevanthi! Wake up!"
 
    The woman who slumbered amongst the trees was the Wood Guardian, Nevanthi, whom Baden had first encountered on the Island of the Banished many years ago. Back then, the solitary Baden had been wandering the length and breadth of Esperia, and happened upon the mysterious island. Suddenly confronted by Graveborn, Baden had readied himself for battle, but was severely weakened by a combination of years of travel, and the inescapable Graveborn curse. He found himself surrounded, before finally falling to the earth.
 
    As Baden came around, he heard a gentle voice by his ear: "Be still. Your Graveborn curse has not yet been fully contained." Before his eyes was a beautiful, delicate woman with a magical rune gleaming from her forehead. The potent breath of life effused from this rune, and followed her hands to brush over his bandaged body.
 
    "Those Graveborn..."
 
    "They are the Tainted, and they are as you: Graveborn who have lost their home."
 
    Seeing that Baden was now fully awake, Nevanthi moved to the side, revealing the Tainted clustered behind her. Their withered faces were beaming with smiles of welcome and friendship.
 
    "Welcome to the Island of the Banished, home of the Tainted."
 
    Accompanying Nevanthi allowed Baden to see the true nature of these denizens of the Island of the Banished. They were totally different from the impression Baden had of Graveborn and, while their features were terrifying, they were possessed of warmth and kindness. In his eyes these Tainted, with their hatred of immortality, were more akin to himself than either humans or the corrupted, fallen Graveborn.
 
    There was peace here equal to that of ordinary human villages, perhaps even more so, as the island avoided the conflicts and turmoil of the outside world.
 
    "You are welcome to stay here, should you so desire." Nevanthi invited Baden with a smile, and yet he did not immediately respond.
 
    "I see you still have someone special to miss. Who are they? Family? Lover? Friends?"
 
    "The closest, dearest friend of my entire life."
 
    Baden did not take up the invitation to settle on the island, but neither did he definitively rule it out. He kept drifting around Esperia, yet would often think of the lonely paradise that was the Island of the Banished, particularly when he quietly gazed out at his homeland from the Lightbearer border. His wanderings occasionally led him back to the island as a visitor, where he would share news of the mainland. He told himself that he visited for brief respite from his curse but, perhaps without even realizing it himself, he began to visit more and more often. 
 
    The day came, however, when Baden paid one of his occasional visits to the Island of the Banished, only to find it affected by Elemental Strife. A miasma of decay covered the entire island, the trees warped and ominous, as a swarm of Corruptors seethed forth from the forest to occupy the once paradise. Nevanthi expended almost all her power to protect the Tainted and fell fast asleep. Before succumbing to sleep, however, she had woven a cage of vines around herself, imprisoning herself in the hope of any eventual rescue.
 
    Baden had not lost his prudence, and realized that rash actions on his part would do nothing but endanger himself and doom the Island of the Banished. Thus he went first to the Dark Forest, where he sought the other Elemental Guardians to assist with the rescue. After meeting with the Wind Guardian, they sneaked back onto the Island of the Banished to execute the plan. The Wind Guardian had staged a diversion to attract the horde of Corruptors, and this allowed Baden, familiar as he was with the island's topography, to reach Nevanthi.
 
    Baden, the weak Nevanthi following, quickly but cautiously moved through the gloom of the forest. The Island of the Banished, once a paradise and refuge for the secluded Tainted, was now filled with scenes of devastation and disaster. Corruptors infest the warped woods, and a single misstep means being surrounded. But as long as they got through the forest to the coast, they would be able to escape the hunt by a departing ship prepared by Baden.
 
    "Don't worry. I will get you out of here."
 
    The elements are already in chaos... I've used too much power to suppress the corruption. Disaster is inevitable... You go find the other Elemental Guardians...
 
    "I'll never abandon a friend." Baden's voice is firm, as when he had saved Thane on the battlefield, "Nevanthi, just hold on. Reinforcements are coming."
 
    The Corruptors were like ants, infesting the woods and impossible to avoid. But Baden keenly sensing a gap in their ranks, broke through with Nevanthi, the Corruptors hot on their heels.
 
    "Reinforcements... You mean that friend you spoke of?"
 
    "We had an agreement. He was to join me here on the Island of the Banished, once the Earth Guardian was found."
 
    The Corruptors tripped and stumbled over the roots and vines which Nevanthi caused to erupt from the earth, but still new ones came, treading on the fallen forms of their fellows in their endless chase.
 
    Suddenly, an enormous monster appeared in the midst of the Corruptors. Its body was fashioned from withered, twisted branches, and the stench of decay filled the air around it. It was an aberration even among the Corruptors, and the source of the island's woes. Vines rotted and decayed in the monster's wake, turning the ground into a putrid bog. It was behind them in a flash, so close it seemed it could just reach out and grab them both.
 
    "I don't think we can wait for reinforcements. You must go, Baden!" Nevanthi despaired at their grim situation, but still she exhorted Baden to leave, saying that at least he could save himself. But Baden did not leave, choosing instead to turn and face the enemy.
 
    "Just hold on. As long as I am here, he WILL come."
 
    The huge monster towered above, looking down at the desperate, stubborn warrior who stood before it, already enveloped in the shadow of despair.
 
    Suddenly a sword of light came screaming down, driving back the huge Corruptor. The dazzling light faded, only to reveal Thane standing before Baden.
 
    Baden asked Nevanthi to retreat into the woods and recover her strength, while he rushed forward to help Thane. He knew that in his present weakened condition, he stood no chance in a direct clash with the monster. Therefore, he kept pace at the side, observing its movements and pointing out weaknesses to Thane.
 
    No match for the monster's strength, Baden and Thane work almost as one. With Baden's support, Thane gradually finds a good offensive rhythm, and is locked in battle with the huge Corruptor. The fight drags on, as Thane is unable to find a killing blow. Facing such a critical situation, Baden decides to take a risk to break the deadlock. He charges, brandishing his bone spear and sawblade, and lands a blow which staggers the giant Corruptor.
 
    Thane sees his opening and strikes, slashing a deep wound open on the monster's chest. However, the injury sends it into a frenzy and, ignoring Thane's blows, it instead charges at Baden, intent on crushing the annoying insect.
 
    Baden is sent flying by the enraged Corruptor. He smashes into the forest while Thane, distracted, is forced to yield ground.
 
    In the forest, Nevanthi braces herself and calls out to Baden. He was already covered in scars, and his constant struggles meant his body was always on the verge of total collapse. With the last of her strength, Nevanthi suspends the Elemental Emblem in the air before Baden. This was her final hope, but it comes at a very heavy cost.
 
    "Baden, my friend... I am powerless to restore your body. However, the Elemental Emblem offers you a chance to... change. If you take it, you are giving up your hard-won peace to become a target of the Corruptors..."
 
    Baden reaches out his hand and grasps the Wood Emblem. Its light totally envelops him, from which brilliance comes calm, resolute words:
 
    "I have only ever known peace in my dreams..."
 
    "It's my destiny to be chased by these shadows..."
 
    "However, I will never fight alone again!"
 
    Surrounded by light, Baden steps forward, his broken body made whole once more through the elemental power of the Wood Emblem. Ahead, Thane and the Corruptor are again locked in bitter battle, a battle which Baden now joins! Thane and he exchange a glance, their years of unspoken understanding rendering words unneeded. Fighting together once more, Thane's wind blades dance continuously, while Baden wields the power of the Wood Emblem to hinder the monster's movements with vines. 
 
    Thane sees his chance and, in a flash, cuts through the energy shield on the monster's chest, exposing a core which shimmers with elemental light. Baden takes over, striking the core with a spear of concentrated wood energy. It is a fatal blow. There's a sudden, violent explosion of energy, and the huge Corruptor falls to the ground with an earth-shaking crash.
 
 
    The battle has settled, and the immediate crisis has passed. But Baden cannot rest. Elemental Strife not only continues, but is getting progressively worse. The remote Island of the Banished will no longer stay untouched by the chaos.
 
    "Let's fight, Thane. Just like the old days."
 
    "Just like the old days."
148.DisplayTips: Ranger. Deploys strength in numbers by summoning a double, and reincarnates himself to boost his endurance significantly. When working with allies with control abilities, he can inflict greater overall damage.

149.Name: CurseCarrier
149.Story: Chapter 1 When Sivi was taken to the huge obsidian obelisk, he felt that the magical edifice before him seemed just like his father: solid and strong. He wasn't Sivi's birth father, however. Both his biological parents had died many years before, in inter-clan conflict. He, and other orphaned children from his clan, had fled here from the invaders like lambs from the slaughterhouse. Even when the one known as the most gifted of the Cursebearers took his hand and led him the whole way across Devotee Square, Sivi couldn't understand why his 'father' had picked him—unexceptional amongst his peers, yet still chosen for this honor. The Cursebearers had always given him the impression of being the most mysterious of the Maulers. They dressed soberly, faces hidden under their cowls, and lived aloof and apart from their own communities in forbidden areas deep within Mauler's Enclave. He also couldn't remember when he first heard the rumor of the curse that flowed through them. His father, however, preferred to call this his 'guardian curse'. Plaintive, struggling cries seemed carried indistinctly on the wind which whistled past his ears. Sivi watched as his father turned around and, with a dull thud, struck the ground with his staff. The powerful waves which emanated from the chunk of obsidian set into the tip of the staff seemed to resonate with the huge obelisk before him. The earth trembled beneath his feet and, while the wind still screamed around him, the other screams subsided. "You should know everything about this place, before choosing to become a Cursebearer." Chapter 2 Salaki had chosen this boy to be his successor for no other reason than that his eyes blazed with more determination than the others. This was the most important trait to possess, once one became a Cursebearer, and was the only thing that could protect you in this place. Here is the very centre of Giant's Jaw, which serves as both the dwelling place of the Cursebearers and the cage which keeps their fate entrapped. Salaki gripped his staff, took the boy's hand, and slowly descended the steps behind the guardian obelisk. Beneath the earth, in ancient pits long since filled, lies buried the cause and source of everything—the mysterious orb known as the 'Ancient Sphere'. It has existed a long time, so long that the precise year it first appeared is lost in the mists of time. Damaged, incomplete records tell of its arrival after traveling the vastness of the universe. They tell how it fell, flaming, from the heavens, and slammed into the primordial plains of Giant's Jaw. Its impact transformed the plains into a valley, flames blazing fiercely for several days before finally subsiding. Salaki turned his attention from the meticulously crafted, mysterious Sphere. His gaze settled on the boy, whose natural wonder at the ancient object, and whose eyes burned with a thirst for knowledge, caused the corners of Salaki's mouth to curve almost imperceptibly. Its craftsmanship and style were truly unlike anything seen before but, even so, it was difficult to trace through known history, even with all the Mauler elders' records. Before the Sphere was completely sealed, Mauler warriors who ventured deep within emerged with items of profound artistry one by one. These were things never before encountered, technology which left them all speechless and which, to this day, have yet to be fully understood. However, opening the Sphere also brought disaster. The warriors who entered the maze inside the Sphere soon began to suffer from hallucinations, even as their bodies withered. Many perished in agony before they could be helped, seemingly similar to the remains of the unknown creatures they had encountered inside. But this was just the beginning. It was only when the general population started displaying the same symptoms that people discovered that the curse, once confined within the Sphere, was now unleashed and spreading through the outside world. To prevent transmission of this viral curse, those who survived buried the Ancient Sphere under earth and stone, and erected a huge magic obelisk of special obsidian to suppress the strange force and hinder the curse from spreading. These individuals volunteered to remain behind, to ensure the safety of all Maulers. As they watched over and maintained the protective obelisk, they absorbed incredible knowledge from within the Sphere, hoping that learning would help them achieve mastery over the curse. Eventually, however, the terrible curse seeped into their bodies, their souls, and even their magic, imbuing it with a corrosive force. Thus were the Cursebearers born. Chapter 3 They had journeyed halfway by the time Sivi took his father's hand and walked through Standfast Hall. His gaze wandered curiously over the crowd. As well as small groups of Cursebearers who were studying or chatting, he saw other children who had already changed into the robes worn by Cursebearers. Others, like him, were following their adoptive parents on the same journey. It was only when he happened to catch the eye of one of his peers that there would be a moment of shared empathy between the children, where they'd smile shyly at each other before looking away. Then Sivi's gaze fell upon a corner of the Hall, where a pale-faced Cursebearer stood alone in the shadows. It was the young woman who had fed and cared for him and his companions when they had first arrived in those lands. She had pulled down the hood which had been covering her face, and was muttering while scanning the crowd. She seemed like she was trying to control some great pain, but a second later her whole face twisted as she began uttering incomprehensible gibberish. Myriad dark curses wrapped around her body before seeping into the ground beneath her feet, spreading out in mottled black streaks. She struggled violently, trying to free herself, but her body was withering at an unimaginable speed. Just as the curse was poised to burn away the last of her life, her eyes flashed with a sudden clarity: "I saw it... I saw that city..." This sentence was her last before she fell deeply into the abyss of madness, screaming hysterically in an ear-splitting howl: "Save me! SAVE MEEE! You cannot escape, oh no no no, there's no escape!" Sivi shrank behind his father, holding tightly onto his robes. His father said nothing, but merely touched his head in reassurance. The surrounding Cursebearers appeared unperturbed, as if used to such sights. Obsidian-tipped staffs shone brightly in unison as they brought the manic Cursebearer under control before escorting her away. The Hall soon became peaceful once more, as if nothing untoward had just happened, but Sivi couldn't get her deranged expression out of his head. She wasn't that much older than he was, but had become a Cursebearer young, saying she wished to suppress the curse here, to protect her clan thousands of miles away. Back when she looked after him, she'd often look at him with smiling eyes, and he felt that something deep inside him had been touched by the now frenzied Cursebearer. His father explained that insanity and screaming were commonplace, whenever the curse they bore grew strong within them. There were even more indescribable things eating away at their bodies, and even their brains, so that those lost control were a real danger to themselves and others. Sivi's father also said that this was the price of being blessed with the power and wisdom of the ancients: to endure the sudden torments of the curse, and those unknown whispers which sounded softly in your ear. It was as if they were all walking a tightrope above the abyss, where a moment's carelessness would be your undoing. Chapter 4 In the land where the Ancient Sphere slumbers, those driven mad by the curse journey to a city within their own consciousness. A remote and unfamiliar city. A magnificent corner of that city seeps out, in which are verdant trees, broad streets, and a variety of exquisite buildings. Colorful lights flash during the day, while airships fly fast or slow in the sky, powered by some kind of unknown energy... This novel, flourishing city scene combines with gentle, cascading sunshine and peaceful, carefree laughter to make all those who see it yearn to join in. However, this lively, joyous scene is actually the curse, penetrating deep into the blood. This is the tragic fate that awaits most Cursebearers, for when they see the city, death is not far off. "Will that happen to you too, father?" The boy looks up as he asks this of Salaki, as they proceed to the final stop of their journey. Once again, Salaki just pats him on the head, but remains silent. They climb the stairs and enter the memorial hall. Here were countless candles burning brightly, as well as wooden alcoves holding many small soul vessels. After the boy had completed the rites of succession, Salaki handed him the Staff of Sacrifice, symbol of the Cursebearers, and hung one of the soul vessels from the wooden alcove around his body. Each vessel represented hope and power, as each contained the indomitable essence of a Cursebearer. Those who had fought against the curse to the very end had transformed their final, flickering light of life into a vital spark, which was then hidden within a soul vessel to await their successors. Watching the boy caress the vessel solemnly, but with reverence, Salaki was reminded of the time when he was still the child named Sivi. After their journey had finished, he couldn't get the images of the young woman and the group of brave, self-sacrificing Cursebearers out of his mind. He decided he wasn't really very good at goodbyes, and that if he had the chance, he would at least try to drag the people he cared about out from their abyss of suffering. His father, whom he respected more than anything, had also delightedly hung the soul vessel for him, the soft words he murmured seeming to contain all his hope for him: "I grant unto you a new name. Henceforth, constancy and integrity will ever be by your side." Chapter 5 Now, it is Salaki's turn to stand before the gates of that city. Hailed as the greatest Cursebearer ever to live, he possessed power far beyond what his father could ever have dreamed of. Yet of them all, he is also the closest to the city. With a deep breath, Salaki pushed open the great main gate of the city with both hands. The magnificent scene within vanished like a phantom of the past, while a vast and nameless shadow loomed in the sky. Sunlight became an impenetrable black fog, which completely enveloped the city. Abominable tentacles emerged from the clouds and twisted around the tops of the buildings. What was once the joyous sound of happiness and laughter became broken but tireless chanting, which mingled in the sudden squall that arose on all sides... "Why us...? Why even we cannot escape...? You're the same, you must be the same as us...!" The unknown curse writhed about him, while the fetid gale hindered his approach. Yet still, with steady steps, did he advance. He was as resolute as when he had become Cursebearer long ago, swearing to be a guardian and protector, and all the countless days thereafter, as he sought life beyond the curse. "We are the guardians of our people, and torchbearers seeking a way out of the abyss."
149.DisplayTips: Support. Unleashes Withering Winds when entering a battle, which weakens enemies while strengthening allies, and delays some of the direct damage received by allies.

150.Name: Bishop
150.Story:
Many years later, when Palmer was ordained as cardinal, he'd recall that distant afternoon when he was 17 and had hastily fled the ball.
 
    Those were Ranhorn's golden years, as the Maulers were locked in unending civil war, the Empire was peaceful and prosperous, and the nobility was intoxicated with outdoing one another in their beautiful clothes, fine wines, and lavish banquets. On this particular day there is yet another charitable ball, attended by all of society's celebrities.
    Palmer, Earl Paggory's young son, stood in a corner clutching his goblet. He had no interest in the ball, but was waiting expectantly for the nobles to shout in alarm. He had been the butt of one of the Lanward brood's jokes on a recent hunt, and had naturally desired revenge. That's why he had just slipped a few drops of a strange potion into the goblet of the offending Lanward, and was thus awaiting the reaction: uncontrollable vomiting, sure to be absolutely mortifying.
    "Urgh..."
    Splendid. It seemed like everyone around him was suitably disgusted.
    "What's this? Quick, someone send for a doctor. Guards! GUARDS!"
    Whatever, the doctor would only think that the imbecile had eaten something bad.
    "Bishop?! Please, wake up, your Lordship!"
    Drat and damnation, how had the goblet ended up in Bishop Giovanni's hand? The old boy was hardly a spring chicken, and had been gravely sick just past year... No, it was just a harmless little prank, the bishop will be just fine... Plus, that Rustport merchant promised it wouldn't really hurt anyone...
    Fear gripped Palmer, who quietly squeezed through the anxious crowd and slipped away from the ball.
    News of the attempt on Bishop Giovanni's life, and his accompanying sickness, spread like wildfire through the capital's outraged residents. Palmer was terrified, and shut himself away at home. He heard from his busy brother that at least a dozen cooks and attendants who had been working the day of the ball had been arrested, and were being interrogated.
    Several days later, Palmer heard that the guards had ultimately decided that one of the servants, recently scolded by the ball's host, had both the motive and the opportunity to ruin the ball, and had thus arrested the poor fellow. Hearing this, Palmer was unable to sit still. He could allow himself to get away with it, but he could not allow another to suffer what was rightfully his own punishment. So it was that he hurried to the guardhouse, determined to hand himself in.
    The captain of the guard listened patiently to Palmer's story then, after a momentary silence, left the room. Palmer sat there, alone and nervous, fully expecting to be escorted off to a cell. He didn't expect, however, for the door to open and his father's furious visage to appear. The guard captain, face plastered in a fawning smirk, motioned for Palmer to follow his father home.
    Palmer refused to let it go. He gritted his teeth before suddenly bellowing in the midst of the guardhouse—and at least ten people were definitely within earshot—confessing his guilt surrounding the poisoning. Earl Paggory's face was livid, and the captain was so embarrassed that, after sneaking a glance at the earl, he forthwith ordered Palmer to be arrested and thrown in jail.
 
    During this month-long incarceration, Palmer was not allowed to see anyone, but could only sit and wait for judgment to be passed. He gleaned a few bits and pieces from his jailer: the wrongly accused servant had been freed; Earl Paggory had paid a hefty sum in compensation, and in hope that the aggrieved party might forgive him. Definitely, his father was still trying to make amends on his behalf, even going so far as to sell off several of the family's properties in order to build a grand new cathedral in the hope that his absurd son might be spared excommunication. He also heard, with relief, that Bishop Giovanni had regained consciousness several days ago, and was slowly recovering.
    It was only now that Palmer realized quite how much trouble he had caused. He was anxious day and night, not knowing quite what his punishment was to be. But then, one quiet evening, his jailer suddenly winked at him while opening his cell door.
    "Go on, hop it. The earl's arranged things for you."
    Palmer was momentarily stunned but then, just as his legs were about to unconsciously carry him from the cell, he couldn't help but ask the guard: "What about you?"
    It was the jailer's turn to be stunned, before mumbling: "The earl gave me some coin... Probably a flogging for me..."
    "No! I've already hurt too many people, I won't allow you to be hurt too." And with that, Palmer hurried back inside his cell and sat down.
    The jailer seemed a little nonplussed, and just left quietly without even locking the door. Palmer stood up hesitantly, but then suddenly spied Bishop Giovanni in a wheelchair, being pushed into the prison by his own father.
    "Your father spoke true. You are not a bad child." The bishop said softly as he looked at Palmer, before turning to Earl Paggory, who had been beseeching him for days, "The Light will guide your son back."
    The earl bowed and left, leaving Palmer and Bishop Giovanni looking at one another.
    Palmer knelt in silence by the bishop's knee, unable to find any words.
    The bishop stroked the crown of Palmer's head, and at the touch Palmer felt warmth flowing into his skull, caused his tense and frayed nerves to finally relax. Then, with sacred light filling the tiny cell, the bishop asked, gentle as if he was sitting in his garden having tea: "My poor boy... Is there anything you wish to tell me?"
    For the first time in two months, Palmer had the chance to speak from the heart. He spoke of his regrets and his fears, of his apologies to those who had suffered, of the shame he had brought upon his family. He spoke too, of his concern that House Paggory had lost its honor, and of the foolish struggle between himself and the young master of House Lanward. They had both thought that those who followed the rules were idiots, while those who transgressed were brave, but they had never stopped to consider that the rules were there to protect everyone.
    Bathed in the sacred light, Palmer covered his face in shame, but Bishop Giovanni gently told him to raise his head.
    "Cover not thine eyes, but follow the light."
    Palmer looked up to see the bishop hand him an old but exquisite copy of church scripture. He took it in silence and looked down, but found the words so strange and incomprehensible that he had to read them multiple times. Finally, embarrassed, he looked up inquiringly.
    Only then did he notice that the bishop had left the cell. Only the light remained, shining on Palmer for a long time.
 
    Palmer was eventually sentenced to expulsion from Ranhorn. Bishop Giovanni himself testified at his trial, asserting that he knew now the error of his ways, and how best to live a good life.
    Palmer did not return to Ranhorn until a full decade later, when Bishop Giovanni had passed away. By that time Palmer was already a member of the clergy, and he stood for a long time before the bishop's grave. He wanted to tell him how much he had learned from the scripture, and how he had been guided by the light for all those years. A gentle breeze blew through the lush green grass of the cemetery, while light fell upon Palmer's shoulders as if in response. And so it was that Ranhorn once more accepted this calm young man, who had found his way back after straying from the path.
    And the scripture, which Bishop Giovanni had given to him, remained by his side for the rest of Palmer's life.
150.DisplayTips: Support. Prays continuously to buff allies while distributing damage they receive to other allies.

151.Name: Mars
151.Story: Veithael was born in the empire to a scholarly family. His father was a scholar of folklore, and a devout follower of the Divine Light, who every evening would regale Veithael with forgotten stories of humans and gods. His enthusiasm also inspired Veithael, who as a child wished innumerable times to become a bard, able to gallop alongside the glorious gods through song, exploring magnificent deeds. Unfortunately, the first Hypogean War broke out soon after Veithael reached adulthood. Hypogeans started appearing everywhere, bringing calamity to humans. Veithael's village was embroiled in the flames of war and his father, mentally and physically exhausted, succumbed to a sudden illness. To protect his home, and repel the Hypogeans, the young, yet hot-blooded Veithael decided to enlist. "Dura and the other gods lead us in opposition, and the Divine Light shall grant us victory!" Thus did Veithael console his mother; until the god of war fell, and despair and the haze of defeat rapidly engulfed the soldiers of the empire. Frequent battles plunged the empire's forces into chaos, but the novice Veithael would not allow himself become disheartened. He still looked after himself meticulously, as he had at home, and as had the gods of whom his father had spoken. The handsome Veithael, with his lustrous blond hair and confident demeanor, cut so dazzling a figure in the barracks that he made those soldiers who had lost their will to fight look weak and incompetent. Cognizant of such a different mentality, the veteran soldiers, worried and terrified, turned their cynical attention onto Veithael, insulting and bullying him. No matter the ones instigating the violence, or those who merely watched, they temporarily forgot their fear in the midst of their wanton cruelty. The young Veithael did not understand that they cursed the light because it illuminated the filth even more. Despite being unable to comprehend this, he bolstered his own spirits by quietly singing ancient songs of the empire, encouraging himself to persevere by remembering heroic deeds, and to become the light which penetrated the darkness of the battlefield. As the Hypogean attacks came ever faster, the years became purgatory. Veithael was the same as the other soldiers, forced to endure one vicious, bloody battle after another. Those battles were dominated by the presence of a particularly powerful Hypogean, possessed of strength which no human warrior could withstand. During one such attack by this Hypogean, Veithael and his comrades were captured and taken to a barren location deep in Hypogean territory. Here had been erected an arena of cruelty, with the supposedly merciful promise that whoever managed to survive would earn their freedom. Some of the soldiers couldn't resist the temptation, and picked the old or weak to face slaughter in the arena. Thus they hoped to win the chance to escape with their lives and vanish into the barren scrubland. The cause of all this evil, the great Hypogean, sat upon his elevated platform and watched the slaughter, feasting each day upon the cries of those in total despair, and growing all the stronger for it. As the number of old and weak prisoners fell, so too did the others' chances of escaping from their hellish existence. Veithael eventually reached the end of his tether too, listening to the whispers of the Hypogeans day after day. Yearning to live, the day came when, holding his shackled hands aloft, he chose another young soldier, just into adulthood, to be his 'sacrifice'. When the young man discovered that he had been 'chosen' by Veithael, confusion and despair clouded his otherwise limpid eyes, in which Veithael saw himself the day he had first enlisted. This brief flash of deja vu was like sharp claws, ripped apart his faltering will as if reopening an old wound. What Veithael was about to do to this young man made him no different than the veterans that had bullied him: people who lost their faith and hope, reduced to nothing but selfish beasts, trampling on the weak to snatch their own, selfish redemption. But at least, right now, Veithael had not taken that final, fatal step into the abyss. Veithael turned around, his once-lustrous blond locks now matted and unkempt, caked in dust and grime. He tried to comb his dry fingers through his hair, before tearing a strip of cloth from what remained of his tattered clothes and tying it back. He strode alone into the arena, singing once more an ancient song of the empire: Oh, how I've wandered far and long; Almost forgetting my home of old; A hundred times did I build my walls; And a hundred times were they trampled down; The beast devoured the old and the young, with terrible, gnashing mouth; It broke my bones and rended my flesh, with awful, razor claws. But oh, I have come home, From the splendid mountain city, the very ends of the world! As the old song rang in the ears of the soldiers, their expressions softened, then became resolute. First one, then another, banged their emaciated fists on the cage as they started to sing along. Oh, the splendid mountain city, wherein the gods do dwell. I take out my bow of gold; My quiver full, I let the arrows of vengeance loose! I drive the blazing chariot of war; Spur on the divine stallions, in my sacred charge! Oh, until my home is rebuilt once more; Oh, I came from these fertile lands, and here too shall I rest! When the Hypogeans arrived to quell the noise, Veithael spoke thus to the great one: "Raising a blade against the weak is the act of a coward. True warriors take on those who are stronger. We are thus destined to win." The piercing defiance in his gaze filled the Hypogean with hate. It flew down, brandishing an enormous sword with which it wished to crush this annoying ant. Veithael averted the blow at the very last moment, deflecting it onto, and breaking, the lock of the cage. Still not finished, Veithael grasped the Hypogean's blade in a deathlike grip. He ignored the blood which streamed from the savage cut, shouting: "Comrades! There is no retreat! We fight the Hypogeans to the bitter end, for our homeland!" Inspired by his words, the soldiers poured out of the cage one after the other. They grabbed weapons and, rushing to his side, fought desperately until the ground was sodden with rivers of blood. They all hoped that this young man might survive, as he seemed destined to bring about great change if he returned to the empire. Less than a tenth of the soldiers survived to return home. When the people once again laid eyes on Veithael, he was nothing but skin and bones, emaciated and weak, but with steadfast resolve still blazing in his eyes. Most survivors stayed as far from the front as they possibly could, but Veithael chose to return to the barracks. Years later, when Ancelot was locked in bitter combat with the Hypogeans in the Frozen Prairie, Lucretia the Betrayed led a sneak attack on Malden, behind allied lines. The garrison suffered heavy casualties, but as the routed forces were being chased and massacred by lower Hypogeans, Veithael appeared, mounted on a golden-armored horse. Again he charged, and again, like a streak of golden light slicing through the darkness. Encouraged, the soldiers gradually reformed their defensive lines, the golden brilliance dispelling their fears in the face of the assault. A forest of spears attacking together easily pierced the Hypogeans' hearts; they were ultimately repelled, and the humans' losses redeemed. Since then, the legend of a well-dressed warrior atop a magnificent steed has spread: he has gorgeous armor and brilliant blond hair, and seems as if he'll stride straight along with the gods. Whenever the blond arrives on the battlefield, the horn of victory blares. The more Veithael showed a presence in a fight, the more soldiers rallied around him, and gradually they became known as the "Golden Bulwark". In the final, decisive battle, the siege of Frost Rift, Veithael's forces held the front line to the very end, driving hordes of Hypogeans into the plight. After the war was over, Veithael received the gods' recognition, thanks to his stellar efforts, and was deified as the new god of war. The historian who recorded this period noted this at the end: mortals are as frail as reeds, but their hearts and deeds can equal the gods.
151.DisplayTips: Tank. Deals huge damage with his Energy Bursts, gains extra max health, and buffs himself and his allies.

152.Name: HML
152.Story:
"On your left! Grab 'em!"
    Hearing the young woman's quiet command, Taya of the Tiger folk stepped smartly over and seized the arm of the "middle-aged man" to his left. He angrily ripped away his fake beard to reveal the panicked face of the woman responsible for cheating them of their money. She'd thought she could slip away unnoticed in disguise, never expecting the young woman to see through her ruse so swiftly.
    "How did you spot her, Mulan?"
    "She still has a lot to learn, if she wants to pass as a man," Mulan said with a smile, before fishing a coin pouch from the swindler's pocket and carefully counting out what was theirs. "Let's go. We can still make it to the market before it closes."
 
    Taya had only met Mulan a couple of weeks previously, when he'd been in a spot of trouble. Taya, his caravan companions, and their wagons had all become stuck in the mud. Unable to move an inch, all they could do was call out helplessly.
    That's when Mulan appeared. A figure, strangely dressed, strode out of the forest, before cleanly slicing through some nearby vines. These were tied to rocks, which were then thrown to rescue the marooned caravans. Eventually the wagons and the crates were also extricated from the muddy trap.
    While the caravaners were out of trouble, the same could not be said of their cargo. The crates were caked in mud, while water had seeped in and soaked the contents. They'd originally intended to sell their goods at the Mutt'Heer harbor, but would never get a decent price now. The caravaners all grumbled and groused with each other, before all seizing on Taya as a scapegoat. They swore they'd been bewitched by a Hypogean into doing business with one of the Tiger folk, as if one of them could become a respectable businessman then steelthorn hens would fly!
    In the end, most of the others left. They took their wagons and share of the cargo, and abandoned Taya, leaving him silent and alone.
    While the caravan may have suddenly disappeared, Mulan had not, and she extended an invitation to Taya.
    "I'm headed for Mutt'Heer Harbor too, as it happens. If you still wanted to go..."   
 
    The pair soon arrived at a small town, where they sold what they had for what they could, purchased new goods, and hit the road again. As they traveled, Taya found himself admiring Mulan more and more: whether she was fetching water, making a fire, or pitching camp, everything was meticulous and tidy. Neither leaking wagons nor wandering bandits could ruffle her seasoned feathers. During one of their evening chats around the campfire, Taya did find out that Mulan had once been a soldier. But she never spoke about where she came from, only saying that it was somewhere far away.
    It took a couple of weeks of trading to recoup Taya's losses, but in recent days he'd been following Mulan's suggestion and purchasing medicinal herbs. The sailors in Mutt'Heer Town often stocked up on such things before a voyage.
 
    Taya had been pretty confident over the past few weeks, by and large, yet the memories of being swindled and bullied kept percolating in his mind. "Perhaps us Tigers really aren't any good at business."
    "No one is ever an expert from birth." Mulan paused but, with no response from Taya, continued: "I don't know what it's like for your people but, where I come from, it was once the case that no women ever went to war."   
    Shocked, Taya listened as Mulan told her tale, of how her father had been conscripted over a decade ago. She had worried that her father was too weak to fight, so dressed as a man to take her father's place on the battlefield. Her military achievements were many, and lasted until the war ended that very year. She refused the khan's offer to become an official, instead choosing to return home. It was only then that her old comrades on the battlefield discovered that she was really a woman.
    Taya finally understand how Mulan had seen right through the swindler's disguise. As someone who had spent a decade living as a man, undiscovered, in the army... Well, there were still some glaring flaws in a seemingly ingenious disguise.
    "That's right. How can your identity at birth determine your entire life?"
 
    It took over a month, and a lot of trouble, for the two of them to finally reach the harbor at Mutt'Heer Town. As they sold their last batch of herbs, Mulan's judgment proved correct: the herbs were a hot commodity, and they made a small fortune from the sailors.
    Taya came over to Mulan as she gazed out at the sea. He recalled that she had been heading for the harbor too, and pointed out where the postal service was: "Look, you can send a letter to your family over there."
    "My family is so, so far away. I doubt my parents would ever receive it." Mulan spoke stoically. "It's even farther than this Lightbearer Empire you mentioned. But what about you? Aren't you going to write a letter home?"
    Taya merely shook his head helplessly, before finally explaining the inherent contradiction and conflict between Maulers and merchants: the Maulers were a warlike people, valuing military prowess and regarding trade as a worthless profession. Both his parents were particularly outstanding warriors, who had sworn as his caravan departed to sever all ties with him... "I'm not like you. You're so powerful I bet everyone in your hometown is proud of you."   
    Mulan heard the envy in Taya's voice, but knew that the customs in her hometown were not as he thought they were. She had also once thought that leaving the battlefield for good and returning home would mean a peaceful life, but had felt uncomfortable soon after getting back. She had been at war for so long that her skills, habits, and even her friends, were all completely different. To her people, the model woman was certainly not what she had become. After a long struggle, she realized that her goal of protecting her father had been achieved, and that it was time to seek another. Thus she had decided to leave once again and, after traveling countless miles, just so happened to arrive in Esperia.
    "You're the only one who can walk your path. That is so much more important than what others think of you." Mulan said, before clapping Taya on the shoulder.
    Taya knew Mulan was right, and that his own problems paled in comparison. From the battlefield to her own home, she had been surrounded by people who didn't understand her, yet had never given in, never capitulated to anything. Taya made his mind up to write an honest, heartfelt letter to his family and, nodding, headed for the post station.
    Mulan watched his retreating back, then turned to gaze back out at the sea.
    So this was the sea... Just like the never-ending plains back home, the wind-whipped waves were like the grass bending in the breeze. Taya will return to his departure soon, maybe I should... set sail for new shores?

153.Name: HFP
153.Story:
"Have you made your mind up, Belinda?"
    In a lava-filled cave deep within the volcanic wasteland of the western Lightbearer Empire, the Fire Elemental Guardian asks the young woman for her final answer.
    Belinda raises her head, exhaustion written on her fair face. Her features are blackened with ash, while her pure white dress is singed and charred by the oppressive heat. Her journey in search of the Fire Guardian had been long and torturous, but her arrival here does not signify an end to her ordeal. The choice she now faced could very well make things even harder, but her steady eyes shone bright with determination:
    "You are not the first to ask me this. Moreover, I've known the answer for a very long time already."
 
 
    A dozen days previously, Belinda had walked hesitantly around the cloisters of the temple, Bishop Palmer's questions still ringing in her ears.
    "Have you made your mind up, Belinda?"
    The peace of the Lightbearer Empire had recently been shattered, when monsters known as Corruptors suddenly appeared in every corner of the land. Even General Rayne had been injured, slipping into a coma from which she could not be awakened. Belinda had tried nonetheless, only to find that the healing power of the Light had no effect on Estrilda or other comatose patients. To make matters worse, the frequency of Corruptor incursions was increasing, with ever more civilians falling before their foul talons. The Temple of Light, always before a place of healing, was now powerless in the face of the comas wrought by Corruptors.
    A spark of hope soon flared, however. The next time Belinda visited Rayne Manor to see how Estrilda fared, a letter from the housekeeper Thane explained the cause behind the current disaster: a catastrophic elemental imbalance, which could only be rectified by finding the five Elemental Guardians.
    She raced back to the Temple and told all this to her mentor, Bishop Palmer. She hoped they might dispatch someone to help scour the volcanic west of the Empire for the Fire Guardian. But Palmer did not immediately grant her request, instead asking if she was sure about her plan, and encouraging her to look deep within herself.
    Belinda understood the Temple's misgivings. To seek salvation anywhere other than the Light would, in the eyes of the laity, be tantamount to admitting the Light's impotence. Insisting on seeking out the Elemental Guardian would also be seen as heresy, and she would be branded an apostate. Distraught, she wondered what else she could do if the Temple refused to help. Suddenly, without even realizing it, she found herself before the door to the Temple, where a commotion brought her back to the present.
    There was a crowd of those afflicted by the disaster, their clothes torn and shabby. Some still clutched small children in their arms as the sisters and brothers of the clergy went among them, handing out bread. When Belinda approached, they noticed her clerical apparel and surged towards her, fervent hope filling their tired eyes.
    A young mother held her child up in front of Belinda, another young victim of the Corruptors. Sadly, this was all too common these days. Belinda knew that the Light had no effect on the afflictions caused by the Corruptors, but also knew that she could not sit idly by as mothers like this looked at her as if she was their final hope.
    Belinda stretched out her hands, letting the Light envelop the child's body. But nothing happened, just like the many other times she had tried and failed.
    The mother fell to her knees, sobbing, as the hope faded from her eyes. Her tears carved two shining paths as they cut through the grime that coated her face: "Is it... Is it because we are not devout enough? I'll dedicate the rest of my life to the Light just please, I beg you... Save my child..." Behind her were countless others, whose gaze swept by the kneeling woman to fall on Belinda.
    She couldn't bear the hope and helplessness in the eyes of the supplicants and made up her mind there and then. There could be no more delay. The Elemental Guardian must be found, and the root cause of this crisis put right.
    "The Light shall protect you."
    Belinda bowed slightly to the despairing crowd, then turned and walked back to the Temple.
 
 
    She burst into his study to find Bishop Palmer sitting with his head in one hand, the other on the desk. He appeared to be examining some important documents.
    "I ask you to let me go to the volcano and find the Elemental Guardian." Belinda broke the silence first. "The elemental imbalance is destroying Esperia's peace. As the priestess of the Temple, I am responsible for thousands of the Empire's citizens."
    Palmer didn't raise his head, but continued staring at the documents before him: "The Light will protect this land, as always."
    "The Light... is not omnipotent."
    Palmer finally looked up, his tone grave as he spoke: "You're treading on dangerous ground, priestess."
    Belinda took a deep breath, aware that she had never before known so clearly what she was going to do. Determined, she speaks resolutely to Palmer: "The elemental chaos must be traced back to its source, and I'm sure the Light will tolerate our pressing need to save people. Please, Bishop, allow me to go at once."
    "The Temple has its own ways to save people. Remember your vows to the Light, priestess."
    "I'm living up to those vows right now." Belinda took a step forward and stood right in front of the desk, looking the Bishop square in the eye, "By the Light above, I will return with hope!"
    Palmer was silent. Ignoring Belinda, he got up without a word and left the study, leaving on his desk what appeared to be an old map. A route was traced on the map, a route which led to the legendary volcano.
    "The Light has always shown me the way," Belinda murmured to herself as she looked towards where Palmer had left. Then, grasping the map tightly, she set out on her journey to the volcano.
 
 
    In the searing heat of the volcano, the Fire Guardian watches the young woman carefully. He saw her perseverance and her faith, but inheriting the Elemental Emblem meant responsibility, and a high price for it: to become the target of the Corruptors, chased endlessly. It was not a decision to be taken lightly.
    "The Light has already written the answer in my heart." Facing the figure in the flames, Belinda seemed to be answering her mentor. "The instant I was ordained, I swore to the Light that I would devote my whole being to my calling, and never abandon anyone who could be saved!"
    The Fire Guardian nodded. "Then it shall be as you wish."
    A mystical rune landed in Belinda's palm, which suddenly burst into violent, surging flames and merged with the pure light that emanated from her. The sacred, golden flames enveloped her, making her seem like a blazing torch that dispelled the darkness and illuminated the dawn. Her hand emerged from the fire, grasping a newly transformed staff.
    The power to save souls was now hers, and she would return bearing renewed hope.
