164.Name: SO
164.Story:
Title: Preliminary Observation Report of Unknown Dead Star 02-21
Category: Interstellar Travel Log
Report Date: Spratmon 23, 1709
Observer: Trishea
Observation Record:
Spratmon 6
    I'd always dreamed of joining the Star Gazers and traveling the universe with my astral form, observing the stars. This is my first time thus traveling, and I was so excited to be able to see all the celestial bodies with my own eyes. Most of these magnificent wonders of the heavens are already in the observation records, however, so I want to push further into the depths of the universe and search for undiscovered marvels.
Spratmon 7
    I have come to the border zone of the Void Realm. Despite being designated a forbidden area by my Star Gazer predecessors, I saw no danger in the place I was observing. Moreover, I believe that a little danger should not put us off exploring the mystery.
    After all, the original purpose of the Star Gazers was to observe the extraterrestrial powers of the universe, in the hope of solving the strange natural disasters occurring on our planet.
    There are not many observation records related to the Void Realm, so perhaps I could stay here a while longer.
Spratmon 10
    All the stars I've observed at the edge of the Void Realm over the past few days are dead, confirming the previous accounts of the Void Realm as a graveyard of the stars. My attempts to communicate have been met with nothing but silence.
    However, just as I was about to call an end to this interstellar sojourn, one of the dead stars I'd previously observed (designated Dead Star 02-21) suddenly responded for a split second.
    In order to gain more knowledge and understanding of the mysteries the stars held, my predecessors had always attempted to make contact with these advanced civilizations. It's hard to believe that all their previous attempts at communication could suddenly produce results here.
    I urgently need to get back and compile my report, let everyone know the good news.
Spratmon 23
    The recorded response from the dead star seems to be imbued with a strange, uncomfortable power, especially after listening many times in my attempt to decode it. I've been so occupied trying to make any sort of headway that I lost all track of time; when I finally returned to my corporal form, I realized that ten days had passed. I was in a strange room, surrounded by solemn elders.
    From them I learned that I had caused alarm during this period—coma, fever, endless recitation in a strange language that no one could understand. My body was getting weaker by the day. It wasn't until they sought out the most powerful mages in the Dark Forest, and they performed an elaborate purification ritual, that I finally regained consciousness.
    But of all that, I have no recollection. I only remember listening to that recorded whisper over and over again.
    After this incident, I looked carefully for any information I could find about the Void Realm, and discovered that I was not the first person to hear those whispers from a dead star. Apparently, prolonged exposure to those sinister susurrations can bring dire consequences.
    The universe is not just filled with romantic stars, as I'd so naively thought. It also holds many unknown mysteries and dangers.
Spratmon 25
    After the purification, I often still fall into a strange, hallucinatory torpor. The elders say this is a residual effect of my experience, and that it will ease with time, but I feel it to be a punishment and lesson from the universe for my previous transgressions.
    I feel sorry and remorseful for my flagrant disregard of my predecessors' warnings. They always said that the Void Realm held chaotic, terrifying forces, but I never took it to heart.
    As a scholar, I should have approached my observations with humility and caution. But this experience has made me truly understand just how dangerous are the extraterrestrial forces we observe and try to comprehend. I don't think I'll be so lucky next time.
    While my view now is different from when I originally joined the Star Gazers, I am still willing to dedicate all my strength to the cause. To prevent Esperia from being corrupted by such a force, and to be fully prepared to resist, we MUST have a thorough understanding of it.
    May the inspiration of the universe always be with you and me, and may the stars ever light and guide our way.
164.DisplayTips: Mage. Able to deal powerful damage and considerable damage buffs and debuffs.

165.Name: SQ
165.Story:
Flickering torches faintly illuminated towering stone slabs. The horde of Arachin warriors, like a forest of swaying trees, were so densely packed that Safiya had no way to retreat. They pressed ever onward, forcing the queen of the Sphinxes to inch closer to the ominous meteorite before her.
 
    Suddenly, the heavy silence was broken by the sneering Ankhira.
 
    "Safiya, is this not your lauded Void Fragment? And look, it's all yours now!"
 
    The arrogant Arachin queen kept up her incessant goading, but Safiya just stared at the sinister Void Fragment in front of her, recalling how she'd been ensnared in the Arachin webs, deep within their nest.
 
    Back then, after being forced from the Sphinx throne by rebels, she'd panicked and fallen into the Arachin queen's lair. Safiya's clever rhetoric and natural eloquence had persuaded the queen to ally herself with her, and she managed to reclaim the throne with the help of her army. But that had also set the stage for her current situation...
 
    The Arachin queen's ambition had been awakened, and no longer was she content to remain in her caves. She led her Arachin army out into Sphinx territory, establishing themselves amongst them in the name of being an ally. At the time, the Sphinxes were recovering from all the chaos, and Safiya herself was busy cementing her renewed grip on power after executing all the rebel leaders. The Arachin queen seized this opportunity to send a huge contingent of warriors deep into the Sphinx domain, causing Safiya to feel threatened by her ostensible allies.
 
    Safiya has originally planned to slowly strip away the Arachin queen's influence and power, but an unexpected incident forced her hand early.
 
    A strangely shimmering meteorite had streaked across the night sky. Following a huge explosion, a fragment was found in Sphinx territory, glittering with terrifying brilliance. Safiya, having practiced the magic of the Void Realm for many years, identified it as a Void Fragment imbued with terrible Void power.
 
    But without waiting for Safiya to investigate, the unchecked Ankhira moved first. She had also sensed the importance of the Void Fragment, and sent soldiers to stand guard, allowing no one to access. Thus did Safiya reveal to Ankhira that the fragment contained the power of the Void Realm, and that if the Arachin queen controlled it, then she too would also gain mastery over its magic. Ankhira's power would make it easy to gain control of the fragment, after which nothing would be able to prevent her from ruling over all Maulers.
 
    It wasn't long before Ankhira informed Safiya of her intention to seize the power of the Void Fragment, and invited her to witness the event.
 
    When Safiya arrived with her escort, she fell into the Arachin queen's carefully laid trap. Hordes of Arachin warriors burst from the shadows and surrounded her. Even worse, her own escort turned against her, drawing their blades on their own queen.
 
    Ankhira hadn't blithely believed Safiya's words, and had always been wary of her ostensible ally. Safiya's unusual behavior aroused her suspicion, and she viewed her as no more than an ambitious politician. If the fragment really was as powerful as she had claimed, then she was certain Safiya would do anything to prevent her from obtaining it.
 
    Ankhira didn't rashly rush to touch the fragment herself, but had some of her Arachins try first. As expected, the second they touched it they were totally corrupted by its dark power, becoming mindless creatures.
 
    This convinced Ankhira that the so-called Void Fragment was a trap, and that Safiya's cordiality had been merely a ruse to leverage the power of the fragment to get rid of her. Information from her spies confirmed this—after all, spiders are the best at spinning webs, and she had long since bought off those Sphinxes who had secretly supported the uprising.
 
    Ankhira was furious at this. Determined to make her would-be murderers pay, she laid the trap and invited Safiya right in...
 
    "We could have shared the throne, Ankhira." The slight tremor in Safiya's voice only made Ankhira's laugh more imperious.
 
    "One throne cannot seat two queens." At Ankhira's nod, several Arachin warriors closed in further on Safiya, forcing her closer to the alien object.
 
    "You're too impatient, Safiya. I may well have fallen for your trap, if you hadn't been so eager for me to touch the Void Fragment."
 
    "You erred in sparing the lives of those fools. Did you really think they'd stay loyal to you?"
 
    "Enough. No more delay. Go now, go and receive power enough to rule the Maulers, Safiya!"
 
    It was impossible for Safiya to refuse Ankhira's 'invitation'; she had no choice but to touch the fragment and its terrible power. Ankhira couldn't hide her joy at every step Safiya took, convinced by the fate of the corrupted Arachins that she too would be consumed by the darkness. This was her golden opportunity to seize control and rule over the Sphinxes.
 
    In the instant that Safiya touched the fragment, a shockwave generated by the huge explosion of pure power hit everyone present. Light burst forth and surrounded Safiya, whose expression was cryptic but calm, a sly smile creeping around the corners of her mouth. The sheer power being released from the Void Realm made her shriek in agony, yet even so, she seemed to be laughing amongst the screams. In a heartbeat, she had vanished into the darkness and the vast space fell silent, as if nothing had just happened.
 
    "Now the Sphinxes have a new queen!"
 
    Ankhira spared no thought for Safiya's disappearance. She wasted no time in ordering the Arachin army to seize total control over the Sphinxes, as their dominion over this foreign tribe was within sight. Her joy, however, was short-lived. The fragment began to shake violently and countless cracks appeared on its surface, from which blood-red light gushed forth to dye the night sky scarlet. Ankhira's quick instincts drove her to hide behind some boulders, away from the light, as those caught in its brilliance were reduced to ashes in an instant.
 
    "Oh, how splendid the forbidden power is."
 
    Safiya reappeared like a faint star in the night sky, enveloped in blazing flames of darkness and with a thunderous unfurling of her wings. Ankhira's eyes widened in disbelief. She didn't know what kind of power it was that could instantly annihilate the army she was so proud of, and return her vanquished enemy to stand before her once again. All she knew was that she had to get out of there.
 
    "Safiya... how...?"
 
    "I never lied to you, my dear, dear ally."
 
    The fragment really did contain the power of the Void Realm, as Safiya had claimed. When she became aware of its existence, she knew at once that she had to have it, as its tremendous power could tip the balance in her favor against her duplicitous ally Ankhira. But if her intentions had been discovered, she knew she'd never be allowed to succeed. Thus had she perversely recommended the Void Fragment to Ankhira, knowing that it would plant a seed of doubt in her heart.
 
    Safiya had even orchestrated the leaking of information. She had deliberately not eradicated all those who had supported the rebels, in the knowledge that they could be manipulated to serve a particular purpose—like passing on misinformation, for example.
 
    All the vulnerability and weakness Safiya had hitherto displayed was solely to mislead Ankhira, and enable her to easily reach the Void Fragment. She understood her ally's character, how Ankhira would always fight an eye for an eye. All the Arachin queen needed was the right opportunity, and she could be counted on to use the fragment to seek vengeance on the queen of the Sphinxes.
 
    "How the tables have turned."
 
    Safiya led the Sphinxes in driving out the remaining Arachins from their territory, winning unprecedented support and trust from the tribe in the process. But securing her throne was not enough for Safiya. Despite having gained phenomenal strength, experiencing such suspicion and betrayal had engendered within her an even greater desire for power. Sooner or later, she would hold sway over all Maulers.
 
    After all, for someone of such ambition, this was just her opening move in the game of absolute dominion.
165.DisplayTips: Support. Her Domains can protect allies, and she gives out Masks to mobilize allies' Energy and focus attacks on specific enemies.

166.Name: BC
166.Story:
Whenever the Ordnance Chief of Bantus is mentioned, the Graveborn would only refer to him as "The Bonesmith" in reverence. Very few know there's an old manual in the corner of his bookshelves, with a barely legible signature of "Ivan" on the cover. Its discernible inside pages contain the following notes.
 
Work #1, Day 1:
Got settled in this small town today. What a wonderful place it is! So many children, simple folks, and everyone is kind and intrigued about me, a new puppet maker. After years of apprenticeship, I finally have a workshop of my own, rather plain, though. But I'm confident in my craftsmanship. I'm sure every child in town will have their favorite puppet soon.
Of course, I'll be making all of them. Hah!
...
Work #117, Day 12:
Luka, the puppy, found a goat's leg bone today. Looking at it, I was suddenly overwhelmed with inspirations! Building the joint like the femoral socket might just solve the problem that's been haunting me! What a good dog! And I'm astounded by such marvelous skeletal structure of goats.
So, could it be the same for human bones, perhaps even better? Heh, what am I thinking... 
...
Work #524, Day 2:
The pastor came to see me today and rudely forbade me from approaching the cemetery behind the Holy Temple in town, all because of unfounded rumors! Andy's parents watched it unfold, glaring angrily at me the whole time. Unbelievable, given little Andy was buried with the puppet I made for him in his arms.
Luka is no longer useful. I must get more components.
...
Work #1744, Day 41:
I can't imagine how my master would feel about what I'm doing, but on top of carving with every tireless chisel stroke, the secret technique I learned from the wanderers near the cemetery also contributed to my creation of intricate puppets, ones even better and livelier than his. Well, at the cost of some secular risks, that's all. I was exiled from the small town, but I didn't care, for it did not impede my working progress. I'm becoming more skilled, and each of my works exhibits greater perfection than the last. What I need...
Are just things people would never need again.
...
Work #2589, Day 1:
When was the last time I ate? Those damned bounty hunters injured me enough that I can't feel my left leg anymore. They barged into my ritual and saved the orphans. I'm sure the kill order from Heresy Inquisition will reach every inquisitor very soon. Now, I'm running out of time and forced to move that concept up the schedule. But if I succeed, it could be a magnum opus for the ages. I finally understand that no one in an ignorant, corrupt state like Lightbearer would ever appreciate my art.
I'm desperate, but I must try.
...
Work #2589, Day 397:
Whenever I eliminated an inquisitor, I'd collect their blade. These so-called sacred blades rang out when I crossed the shady borders of Bantus, announcing my arrival to the realm of Graveborn. No Graveborn stopped me. They made way for me with awe and respect in their eye sockets. As for the whispering necromancers... I knew the supreme masterpiece, the puppet shell in which I was reborn, was the object of their obsession. Learning of my presence, The Fallen King ordered soldiers to lead me to the Court of Bantus, where my skills and aesthetic shall finally find a home.
 
"Those who couldn't be my audience ultimately became my work of art."
166.DisplayTips: Support. Ivan generates a Spirit Shield that protects allied heroes and enhances their damage output. He can also sculpt a Skeletal Squire to undermine the enemy.

167.Name: SWQ
167.Story:
In the desert, Rhett the bandit leader and his crew cheered loudly. They had just plundered a shipment of valuable silver, which was even now jingling in sacks strung across saddles.
    Suddenly, they all felt the sand shift strangely beneath their horses' hooves. In a flash, both steeds and men were trapped in a sandpit! Just then, out from the sea of sand jumped a little girl with strange braids and bells sown into her sleeves! She was supported by a huge Wyrmcrawler, so thick that two men would barely be able to get their arms around it.
    The girl's face was flushed with rage as she scolded them loudly: "TOO NOISY!"
 
    Exquisite silver items gleamed brightly in the blazing sun, but Naroko just kicked them aside. These jerks in front of her had not only disturbed her lovely nap in the cave, but had also tried to attack her Wyrmcrawler Nadia! It was only when Nadia had them trapped in swirling sand that they begged for mercy, and thought to curry favor with these shattered pots.
    "There's no candy in the pots!" Naroko was still fuming. These guys deserved to be turned into jerky in the searing desert sun! She rang a bell, summoning Nadia and preparing to return to her cave.
    "We have lots of delicious things in our camp!" Rhett said quickly, "We only parted from our Wyrmrider friends last month, and wasn't expecting to bump into you today... It was all just a misunderstanding!" 
    "You met the Wyrmriders?"
    Seeing the hint of expectation in Naroko's otherwise nervous expression, Rhett knew he'd guessed right. The Wyrmriders were a mysterious tribe who lived deep in the desert; while short, they had the ability to control Wyrmcrawlers—commonly known as giant sand worms. They had always lived in seclusion, and this little girl in front of them must have been accidentally separated from her tribe.
    Still trapped in the sand, Rhett's smile never left his face: "Of course. We traveled together for half a month..."
    Before he'd finished speaking, there was a surge in the sea of sand, and the bandits found themselves standing on firm ground once again.
 
    Night had already fallen by the time Naroko arrived at the camp with Rhett and the others. He had promised to tell her in which direction the Wyrmriders had gone, as long as she had Nadia stir up quicksand to trap caravans for them. Naroko was so excited that she didn't mind the simple dinner, but Nadia seemed a little restless, shaking her toothed head and nuzzling Naroko's leg.
    Just then, Naroko remembered there was still business to take care of, and had Nadia lie down. The bandits didn't understand what she was doing, and could only watch as she stuck a hairpin from her braid into Nadia's body! The giant wyrm shuddered, then curled into a ball.
    The bandits let out a low murmur of surprise and glanced at each other.
    Naroko was a little surprised when she saw their nervousness, and asked: "Don't you know? The hairpins of my people are all highly toxic, which is how we can control Wyrmcrawlers."
    "Oh yeah, that's right. It's been a few days, I'd almost forgotten." Rhett mumbled vaguely as he sat beside her. He avoided the hairpin that Naroko had pulled out as he handed her a chunk of bread.
    Naroko took it with one hand as she patted Nadia with the other and asked, "Have you got any dragonberries? I'm sure you know how much Wyrmcrawlers love them."
    Rhett stroked his chin, and immediately promised to share all future dragonberries with Naroko.
    "Okay." Naroko said, and took a big bite of her bread.
 
    "There's a large caravan, just a few dunes away." Under the blazing sun, Naroko stroked Nadia, who had just wriggled out from a sand dune, and shared the news. "Nadia's already sensed their vibrations, so we should probably hurry under through!"
    Rhett considered briefly, then suggested that Naroko and Nadia go first and trap the caravan, after which he and some of his men would follow on horseback. Naroko disagreed, saying that she was worried about getting separated from everyone in the desert, and insisting that they all go together. Rhett complained, helplessly, that they had no way of traveling under the sand.
    Realization suddenly flashed across Naroko's face, and she quickly rang another bell, whereupon Nadia began to writhe before spitting out a large glob of mucus.
    "Just rub this on your body, and you'll be able to breathe through your skin under the desert." Naroko giggled, "Didn't my people ever do this with you before?"
    "Well, we were all busy rushing back then." Rhett said no more, but reached out a hand towards the stinking mucus.
    Everyone followed Nadia beneath the desert sand, but Rhett very quickly began to feel suffocated. The mucus on his body made the sand stick to him even more, and gradually became unable to move. He looked around for Naroko in desperation, but couldn't find her.
    Rhett would never have the chance to learn that the domesticated Wyrmcrawlers didn't need to eat at all, or that the hairpins of Wyrmriders contained no poison. On the contrary, the Wyrmriders sustain the Wyrmcrawlers with their own strength. What really was poisonous, however, was Wyrmcrawler mucus...
 
    Several miles away, Naroko was still furious at being cheated yesterday.
    "Hard working spitting up all that venom! Ripping them to shreds would have been okay too, but it's more fun this way..." Naroko put her arms around Nadia's neck. "Come on, let's go back and have a nap!"
167.DisplayTips: Tank. A highly protective hero who raises a summoned entity that absorbs damage, heals allies, and taunts enemies to reduce damage they deal.

168.Name: Lucilla
168.Story:
"Curses! The gods will arrive any moment, and our weapons are barely at half-strength..." Despite his despair, the alchemist sealed the two weapons in a specialized metal container. A button press sent them deep into the earth, hidden by intricate layers of mechanisms, shielding them from divine scrutiny. Beyond the laboratory, the gods breached the final defenses. Amidst the cacophony of death and ruin, the alchemist's heart stilled.
    Left without any desire to resist, he calmly awaited his end.
    "Wretched gods... These weapons shall never be yours. Mark my words, your end is nigh. When they reach their full power, humanity will step over your decayed remains and forge a legacy of everlasting glory!"
 
    After two millennia, the metal container resurfaced in the hands of a grinning Hypogean named Eugene. "Well, well, what a surprise! These are the powerful weapons coveted by the gods?!" Within the container lay two swaddled infants, a boy and a girl.
    Beside the Hypogean stood the Celestial Gavus, an unforeseen travel companion. His mission was to reclaim these weapons, taken by the Hypogeans long ago, but the current scene puzzled him. "The gods may exploit these children. We can't allow them to become their pawns."
    Eugene's gaze held contempt. The allure of ultimate power seemed to make gods no different from Hypogeans.
    Unexpectedly, the girl started crying and flailed her arms angrily. Conversely, the boy merely babbled and offered smiles to the new onlookers. In truth, they appeared indistinguishable from human children.
 
    Three years seemed to pass in the blink of an eye. Deep in a remote forest, a brother and sister played merrily while two men watched them quietly from afar.
    Ultimately, Gavus and Eugene abandoned their factions, spiriting the children away into the forest, away from their warring kin. There, they became fathers to the youngsters, naming them Liberta and Lucilla.
    The children's natures were near-perfect opposites, akin to the two men who embraced them. Lucilla inherited Eugene's cunning mischief, while Liberta embodied Gavus' solemn discipline. This unlikely family resided peacefully in a secluded realm, untouched by the flames of warfare.
    However, their tranquility was short-lived. The Celestials and Hypogeans persisted in finding these living weapons and their renegades. Eventually, they located the family's haven, and this time... they prevailed.
 
    A decade later, a girl carried a colossal red axe, guiding a team of Hypogeans through long-forgotten ruins—an ancient alchemist's lab. Here, potent weapons were infused with divine energy. Lucilla aimed to harness that same power. On the ruins' opposite side, a faction of Celestials, sharing the goal, assembled. As the ruins reawakened, the two groups geared up for a reenactment of a historical battle over magical reserves.
    Years ago, the Hypogeans abducted Lucilla. Her memories were sealed, and she turned sinister under their sway, becoming into a powerful asset for their faction. As she surveyed the Celestial ranks, Lucilla sought their leader. She eventually spotted him—a young Celestial boy holding a mystical staff.
 
    The earth quaked as the ruins awakened, reigniting the battle for its power. Amidst the surge of the laboratory's energy, Lucilla bounded toward the Celestial command center, set on swiftly defeating her adversaries. Suddenly, a figure burst forth from the Celestial ranks, intercepting her aerial attack. They engaged in a fierce clash, and Lucilla was stunned to find herself evenly matched with her opponent. To make matters even more confusing, the young boy emitted an inexplicable familiarity she couldn't fathom.
 
    With each strike, the strange sensation intensified. Unable to endure it any longer, Lucilla marshaled her magical might, poised for her ultimate strike. In tandem, the young Celestial soared into the air, mirroring her stance. Like fiery meteors, they clashed in the sky. The collision shattered the seal imprisoning Lucilla's memories, and her first utterance was her brother's name, "Liberta!"
 
    Finally reunited, the long-lost siblings recognized each other, shifting their attacks at the final second. The resulting blast hurled the ruins into chaos, providing their escape route. Unshackled from their factions, Lucilla and Liberta began their most vital quest: to recover the two missing pieces of their once-happy family.
 
    "Let's go, Liberta! We're gonna make them pay for what they did to us!"
168.DisplayTips: Support. She chases enemies persistently and seals their attributes. She can also create domains around herself, and enemies within the domain cannot gain shields.

169.Name: Liberta
169.Story:
Liberta wasn't born a god. In fact, his birth was a rebellion against the gods. Two millennia ago, during the Age of Arcana, human civilization flourished. Led by the warlord Gaius, humanity waged war against the gods. To strengthen their cause, an unnamed alchemist conceived a prohibited rite that converted ordinary people into god-like weapons. Liberta and his sister Lucilla were such weapons, referred to as "Dawn" and "Dusk."
 
    Yet, these weapons demanded significant magical energy. In response, Gaius instructed his forces to build the Cradle of Truth, a unique facility. As the Cradle's magic reserves reached their zenith, the dormant power within the siblings would awaken, bestowing them godlike abilities.
 
    Ultimately, the plan failed. News of these "weapons" leaked before they were activated. The gods assaulted the Cradle of Truth, and the Dawn and Dusk were sealed in an arcane container by the alchemist, destined to be reawakened in the future.
 
    Two millennia had passed, and the Celestials rediscovered the container, which was then swiftly intercepted by the Hypogeans. Through a convoluted and often violent series of exchanges, the container wound up with an unusual pair: Celestial Gavus and Hypogean Eugene. Freed from their confinement, Dawn and Dusk opened their eyes to see the men before them. Yet, the oddity of their peaceful unity remained lost on them. In fact, Liberta naturally smiled at them as if they were his parents.
 
    Gavus and Eugene were stunned by the revelation of that these weapons coveted by their factions were infants. Originally, Gavus sought to regain favor among the Celestials by recovering them. Over time, though, he forged a strong bond with Eugene and the two siblings. They couldn't possibly regard these innocent children as instruments of war, yet their factions remained unconvinced. To protect them from the conflict, Gavus and Eugene withdrew from the war, spiriting the children away. Amid their escape, danger and death loomed. Still, they ultimately eluded their pursuers, finding refuge in a remote corner of the Dark Forest.
 
    Gavus and Eugene adopted the children as their own, renaming them. "Lucilla, for a life illuminated with brilliance and grandeur. Liberta, for a life brimming with freedom and the power to carve his own destiny."
 
    Those were the most joyful days in Liberta's life. He had a name and two devoted fathers, despite their differing personalities. Arguments between Gavus and Eugene were frequent, yet trivial.   
 
    Eugene, the sly Hypogean, delighted in hatching tricks aimed at Gavus. Paradoxically, his well-thought-out pranks often floundered against the unyielding Gavus, backfiring remarkably.
 
    With time, young Lucilla became Eugene's accomplice in mischief. She mirrored his cunning, spending hours devising methods to vex Gavus. Prior to executing their pranks, Lucilla ensured that her honest brother, Liberta, wouldn't warn their father. Gavus, however, proved challenging to deceive, leading to frequent punishment for their scheming—Liberta included, for not telling the truth.
 
    Under the watchful eyes of Gavus and Eugene, the siblings blossomed into happy, healthy children. However, their peaceful lives were fleeting. By the time the pair reached three years old, the united forces of Celestials and Hypogeans had found their refuge and launched a pursuit.
 
    Gavus and Eugene fell into the clutches of their factions, facing identical fates: lifelong imprisonment. Lucilla and Liberta were also separated from one another and had their memories sealed away. Soon, they began training as hidden weapons in the age-old Celestial-Hypogean conflict. Both sides eagerly awaited the day when the Cradle of Truth would be reactivated.
 
    A decade later, as the Cradle of Truth reawakened, Liberta led his Celestial comrades toward it. On the opposing end stood Lucilla, commanding her Hypogean forces, poised for swift action. With the Cradle fully powered, both factions surged forward, vying for its magical energy. Liberta and Lucilla dived headlong into the fray.
 
    As the siblings confronted each other, their combat intensity spiraled uncontrollably. Having absorbed immense energy from the Cradle of Truth, Liberta and Lucilla unleashed their ultimate strikes. The clash created a shockwave, violently shattering the battleground and shrouding it in dust and debris.
 
    The Celestials and Hypogeans ceased their fighting and stared intently, waiting for the cloud of dust to settle and hoping to see their secret weapon emerge from within.
 
    As the dust cleared, hope faded for both sides. Liberta and Lucilla had vanished. Only the shattered remains of the Cradle of Truth could be seen. Unexpectedly, the seals of memory had broken during their clash. Recovering their memories, the siblings redirected their attacks and fled amid the chaos. Reunited, the long-lost siblings still lacked two vital family members.
 
    "Liberta, it's time to show them what we can really do!"
169.DisplayTips: Support. Linking ally and enemy, he can heal and dish out damage. When fighting alongside his sister, his potential will burst forth.

170.Name: AstroPOM
170.Story:
As the leader of the Dusk Patrollers, Lyca encountered an extraordinary trial. Her bond with the sky weakened, and the starry power she relied on vanished. Enveloped by darkness, taunting jeers and hushed murmurs converged as if planned from the start.
    —"Without the power of the stars, how can she possibly be a commander."
    —"Just give up already. Let someone more capable assume command."
    Amidst this dark illusion, the more Lyca struggled to flee, the louder the mockery resonated. Whispers from all sides entangled her, like muddy tendrils crawling up her body, pulling her toward the abyss.
    Not too long ago, a foreboding meteor crashed into the heart of the Dark Forest. It ignited an evil blaze, acting as a portal for the Hypogeans to invade. The clanspeople's minds were also ensnared by the shadows. On her spirit deer, Lyca skillfully threaded through lakeside thickets. Her objective was to rendezvous with Dusk Patrollers on their mission to locate the void fragment.
    Unbeknownst to her, a sinister aura concealed within the thickets seized her mount's galloping hooves with malevolent force. Lyca tumbled, and the inky darkness consumed her. In the blink of an eye, her spirit deer vanished without a trace.
    Alone in the boundless darkness, Lyca ran with all her might, desperately shaking off the constraints that ensnared her. Yet, no matter what she did, the darkness remained an ever-present shadow. Gradually, she slowed her steps, the faces of every clan member in the forest flashing through her mind.
    Lyca had always felt that it was the power granted by the stars that allowed her to thrive on the battlefield, repelling the Hypogean threat. Now, with that power taken from her, even if she escaped this ordeal, she dreaded facing the hopeful eyes of her clan members. Could she still lead as their commander, protecting kith and kin?
    "Will I be left with nothing once I've lost the power of the stars?" Lyca whispered, darkness slowly spreading across her face. In a fleeting moment, she remembered the counsel given to her by the forest sage when she was first graced by the presence of the star spirit: "My child, amidst the dazzling starlight, you must see your path clearly."
    At that time, she had interpreted those words as needing to rely on the stars and their power to earn her clan's trust, a requirement for becoming a leader of her people.
    Yet long before the arrival of the star spirit, she had already embraced the role of commander. To live up to this duty, she trained tirelessly, adapting tactics based on the strengths of each Dusk Patroller, intent on unleashing their potential in battle. This way, they could ensure survival even in the face of their mightiest foes.
    It wasn't her magical powers that won her the trust of her companions, but rather her skill in uniting and guiding them to victory against all else.
    As the meteor struck the Dark Forest, Lyca swiftly delegated tasks to her men. From controlling the fire and repelling Hypogeans to caring for wounded comrades, their actions, directed by her, were swift and precise. Their coordinated efforts dispelled the forest's encroaching darkness.
    "...Even if I don't possess the power to light up the sky, I can still lead everyone towards where the light shines."
    Lyca's eyes snapped open, her voice resolute as she tore apart the muddy restraints closing in on her. The severed bond with the star spirit appeared to rekindle with each resounding heartbeat within her chest.
    The darkness retreated, replaced by thick mist, as the Hypogean revealed its colossal, single eye. The illusion it had woven shattered, and a snow-white doe materialized. It landed beside Lyca with grace, tenderly tending to her injuries. The radiant aura of the doe scattered the darkness in every direction.
    Enveloped in the soft radiance emitted by the star spirit, Lyca's eyes turned resolute and unshakable. "I won't depend solely on the power of the stars any longer. Now, I'll take the first step on the path I've chosen for myself."
    Cries of agony, furious roars, and mournful howls burst forth from the Hypogean's mist-like body. Its black tendrils surged toward Lyca, attempting to bind her once more.
    —"Don't delude yourself! You will save no one! These lands are destined for darkness! Only destruction awaits!"
    Several stars heeded Lyca's call, descending with long tails trailing behind them from the shattered rifts. In Lyca's hands, they converged into a massive bow.
    "I am the commander of the Dusk Patrollers."
    She pulled back the longbow, and a powerful beam of starlight gathered at the arrow's tip.
    "When one loses their light, I shall be the Dawnbringer that offers them hope!"
    A brilliant light pierced the ominous aura of the void fragment, erupting from the lake's center and lingering in the sky for a shining moment.
    The darkness receded, replaced by gentle starlight that embraced the lake's surface, casting a glow rippling outward. In the forest, those to whom Lyca had assigned tasks remained dedicated to halting the disaster's advance, finding inspiration in one another's efforts.
    On the horizon, as the fierce fire ebbed, the first light of dawn appeared.
170.DisplayTips: Ranger. She can move while dealing Normal Attacks and also inflict damage on multiple enemies at once.

171.Name: Admiral
171.Story:
The young lad stirred from his slumber. Carried by Jerome after succumbing to hunger, he awoke to the smell of grilling fish. The aroma wafted through the air, capturing the young boy's senses.
    "Join me. The fish is ready," Jerome signaled, holding up their roasted meal. Approaching forty, it had been a decade since he was in command of the Thousand Sail Fleet. The boy instinctively felt for the stones beside him. His captain and fellow deckhands had told him that if he ever encountered the Imperial Navy, he must find a way to take them out.
    "Hungry?" Jerome glanced at the boy. "We're stuck on this forsaken island, so it doesn't matter if you're a pirate or a marine..."
    Although the lad was doubtful, his rumbling stomach responded in kind.
    "You can call me Captain Jerome," he said, handing the boy a cooked fish.
    Upon hearing the man's name, the boy hesitated slightly before taking the fish and tearing into it.
     "So you've heard of me..." Jerome asked.
     "Everyone knows Jerome, the Navy Pirate," the boy replied. "Our captain mentioned that you kept chasing us for months. Craftier than the most devious pirates, he said."
     "Ha! I'll take that as a compliment," Jerome chuckled, biting into his fish with a grin.
     "Do you remember where you're from?" The older man continued.
    Jerome knew all too well where boys like these came from. He, himself, was once a deckhand on the pirate ship Peg Leg. He knew what it was like to be taken and put to work by merciless pirates. If he was lucky, he might live to see thirteen and become an official member of the crew. This child must have come from a small fishing village, from some humble and unremarkable family.
     "No..." the boy said quietly.
    Erasing these kids' pasts – that's the tradition on the Peg Leg, Jerome remembered.
    Jerome looked at the young lad and asked, "How old are you?"  
     "Eleven, twelve, maybe."  
    The older man spat out a fishbone as he spoke. "No need to lie, lad. I'd reckon you're at most nine."  
    The youngster had already finished the roasted fish and sat there awkwardly. Jerome gestured that he could have more.
     "If we manage to get out of here, is there anywhere you wanna go?" Jerome asked him.
     "I don't know." Jerome could see tears welling up behind the boy's eyes, hidden behind each ravenous bite he took.
     "Listen, your captain is dead. You don't need to go back to that life anymore," Jerome said reassuringly.
    After being given command of his own ship, Jerome had been searching relentlessly for the Peg Leg. This infamous pirate ship had sown chaos along the Empire's shores, leaving destruction in its wake. It had separated this young boy from his life, much like it had done to a young Jerome many years ago when his village was raided and razed. That time, the Empire responded by sending three warships to pursue the Peg Leg. However, the pirate captain was able to distract the pursuing navy by throwing his deckhands overboard one by one. Jerome was among the handful who managed to survive the ordeal.
    From that time on, Jerome's sole wish was the Peg Leg's demise. By day, he manned sails and oars beside the crew. By night, he grappled with illiteracy, striving to learn. He barely managed to graduate from the naval academy. Yet he ascended, moving from midshipman to lieutenant and finally becoming the captain of his own ship. Jerome, not confined to doctrine, knew defeating pirates meant thinking as they did. Fellow captains saw an oddity—pirates saw a nemesis. Recently, he had caught wind of the whereabouts of the Peg Leg. Through misty seas and perilous reefs, he chased, crafting detailed plans, until the Peg Leg found itself in a corner with no escape.
     "In the end, I never thought that damn pirate would resort to blowing up the Peg Leg just to try to destroy me and my ship. I guess that was his final lesson. I searched this island for three days, and you're the only one I found alive..." Jerome's voice was tinged with regret. He could have saved more children.
     "If you have nowhere to go, you can join my fleet," Jerome offered. The boy looked at him, confused.
     "At the very least, you can attend the naval academy. Once you graduate, you can join my ship. Maybe even be my first mate one day. I think you'll be an officer in the future." Jerome said with a hearty smile.
    "Naval academy..." "First mate..." These words danced in the boy's imagination. He began to dream of a future worth living.
     "Can I really?"  
     "Absolutely! The navy always needs a few good men, and everyone has something to offer!" Jerome stood up straight. He lifted the canvas behind him. "This rowboat is still intact. We can use it to leave this forsaken place."  
    Leading the boy to the shoals, they managed to push the small boat out to sea as they climbed aboard.
     "I have a feeling this dinghy is about to save two people that will change the course of history. What's your name, son?" Jerome said as he paddled.
     "I'm Nate."  
     "Well, Nate, from now on, you are a member of the Imperial Navy. Stand tall!"

172.Name: Robin
172.Story:
Cindy sat nervously in the corner of the stage, her frozen limbs slowly thawing in the warmth of the fire. This was a special performance dedicated to Lord Lakovy. All the attendees were wealthy, with one exception—her. Cindy cautiously peeked out from behind the curtains and saw Lord Lakovy sitting in the very center of the front row. His fingers gently caressed the exquisitely crafted golden brooch on his chest.
    She instinctively withdrew. The theater dimmed unnoticed. A young man stepped into the center of the stage, a spotlight suddenly shining down on him. He doffed his hat, offering an exaggerated bow to the audience, and the curtains began to part slowly.
    The performance had officially begun.
  
    Cindy should have been on her way back home with the pay for her errands, perhaps picking up a couple of loaves of black rye bread. However, the steward had no time to see her. He was too preoccupied with preparations for the master's event.
    But Cindy already knew that even without this excuse, Lord Lakovy would find other reasons to withhold her wages. He never cared whether his workers had food in their bellies. He only cared if his coffers grew fatter that day. But she couldn't wait until tomorrow. In this frigid weather, her grandmother, lying in bed, would not survive the night.
    This town, near the frontier, had a small population but vast farmlands. Once self-sufficient, everything changed with Lord Lakovy's arrival. Initially, he hired many farmhands to build his manor, keeping townspeople busy while quietly taking control of the surrounding lands. With less homegrown food, people had to work for Lakovy to eat. Soon, he controlled most of the grain, driving prices high and wages low. Eventually, everyone was too drained to resist.
    In the play, the youth climbed a tree branch to survey and rally his comrades. Hiding behind a tree by the forest road, he expertly shot arrows, puncturing grain sacks on passing carriages. Outlaws swiftly gathered and shared the spilled grains with the poor. It was the tale of a heroic outlaw in Sherwood Forest, aiding the oppressed to gain freedom by toppling exploitative nobles and landlords to return their ill-gotten wealth to the common people.
    Cindy observed, entranced, yearning for a hero like him to help the people here. She wouldn't have needed to stand outside trembling, waiting for Lord Lakovy to come out after the show. If she hadn't encountered the lead actor coming in, she might have succumbed to the freezing winds.
    The young man had listened patiently as Cindy told her story. Unfortunately, Cindy couldn't make out his face, hidden beneath the brim of his lowered hat. But more than his looks, she remembered the green cloak he took off and draped around her shoulders, along with his kind words.
    "Things will get better for you," the young man said. "How about you stay and watch the show?"
 
    The Megamouth Shark Troupe, a renowned resident theater company in Oakenfell, consistently had sold-out shows. Cindy yearned to see them, but they never toured small towns like this. In fact, if someone claimed to be the Megamouth Shark Troupe, no one here would know the difference.
    But this time, to curry favor with Lord Lakovy, someone had specially invited the Megamouth Shark Troupe to perform here.
    The show was superb, earning thunderous applause. The youth displayed impeccable crossbow skills, never missing a shot. He even split an arrow down the middle, striking a second already in the bullseye.
    Lord Lakovy stroked his brooch, his expression darkening with discontent. As the young man condemned the villainous nobles, Lakovy's face nearly matched the color of the actor's hat. In the performance, just as the actor was passing judgment on the nobles, he was struck from behind. A nobleman's guard, feigning injury, delivered a "deadly blow" when the actor turned his back.
    Cindy gasped and covered her mouth. But Lord Lakovy leaped up, loudly cheering the "shameless thief's demise". Scattered, hesitant applause followed from the crowd. Suddenly, an arrow whizzed past Lakovy's head, pinning his wig to the tent wall.
    Though the actor had "fallen", he told his comrades to bury him under the cypress tree where the arrow had dropped. Through that tree, which leads to the underworld, he would return when injustice again ran rampant in the land.
    As the actor spoke his final line, the stage lights dimmed, and the curtains fell. Lord Lakovy grunted and resumed his seat, begrudgingly satisfied with the ending. These so-called outlaws were just poor thieves who couldn't survive otherwise. Their deaths served justice and order, as they should.
    Thinking this, Lakovy forgave the "farce" of a play. Twirling his mustache, he hummed a smug tune and unconsciously reached for his brooch.
    In the darkness, an enraged roar shattered the silence:
    "Where is my brooch?!"
  
    A carriage that was racing raced to a street corner several kilometers from the theater and came to a halt. The young man lifted Cindy down, handing her a heavy little sack that was filled to the brim with gold.
    A second carriage loaded with gold and grain rounded the corner. Cindy recognized it was coming from Lakovy's manor.
    "Run along now and put that money somewhere safe. Don't stop until you get there."
    The young man gave Cindy's shoulder a gentle push, and she took off running home. Glancing back, she saw him tossing something up and down as he climbed into his carriage - the intricately crafted golden brooch glinting blindingly in the sunlight.
    "Will I see you again?" Cindy called out eagerly.
    The young man laughed softly. He tossed the golden brooch into the pile of grain, pulled down his hat brim, and the carriage wheels began turning.
    "As long as greed and injustice remain, I won't be far away."
 
    "He will risk everything for the sake of justice. That is Robin Hood." —Arthur

173.Name: Calypso
173.Story:
Crash! The door burst open, and a frail woman rushed into the room.
    In the secret workshop of the Bonesmith, countless puppets littered the corridors, their cries of anguish filling the air. Shemira felt the souls' wails within the puppets, witnessing their past lives. These poor souls suffered, their bodies turned into puppet shells, their spirits imprisoned to obey the tormentor. Yet the Bonesmith remained unsatisfied, deeming his creations defective, seeking more victims to torture.
    Shemira sadly shook her head, pulling herself from the painful memories of these tortured souls. She needed to find Daimon swiftly, or else...

    In the workshop's depths, the Bonesmith carved a puppet's joints. Daimon lay motionless on the dissection table nearby. The Bonesmith, displeased, mumbled, "Something's missing... No matter, once I unlock this boy's hidden power, you'll all be perfect masterpieces!"
    "Give Daimon back to me!" Shemira shouted as she charged forward.
    Surprised by the intruder, the Bonesmith waved his hand casually. As if pulled by invisible strings, the puppets around the room suddenly sprang to life and attacked Shemira.
    "This is no ordinary child," the Bonesmith laughed manically. "Once I unravel his secrets, countless masterworks will be born!"
    "I won't let you!" Shemira yelled furiously. "I heard the cries of these souls. I know what you did to them. I won't let you do the same to my Daimon!"
    Shemira desperately fought off a puppet. But the puppets easily reassemble, continuing their onslaught even when broken. Shemira's attacks met only air.
    While watching Shemira's struggle, the Bonesmith condescendingly shook his head. How could this woman grasp his grand vision? Sneering, he approached Daimon with a carving knife. Panicking and distracted, Shemira was hit by a puppet and fell.
    Trapped beneath the tangled puppet limbs, Shemira reached out desperately for Daimon, letting out a despairing wail. Daimon stayed unresponsive, just like when he lay in his coffin before, unmoving despite her tears.
    "I've lost Daimon once already, I won't let it happen again..."
    "You're not taking Daimon away from me!"

    "I hear your pain," Shemira called out to the puppets. "Give me your strength, let me avenge you."
    A puppet froze in its tracks. After a moment, its bones rattled as a tortured soul wrested free from the puppet's husk and seeped into Shemira's body. The soulless puppet collapsed limply into a pile of bones.
    Shemira rose unsteadily to her feet, as more and more souls converged and melded into her.
    "You're mad! The spirits will consume you! You'll become a mindless monster!" the Bonesmith shrieked in terror.
    The overwhelming resentment raged within Shemira, the torment rendering her speechless. Boundless hatred engulfed her entirely, and a roar that was not her own erupted from her throat:
    "You shall perish!"

    A long chain crackling with vengeful energy formed around Shemira. She flicked her wrist, and the chain shot toward the Bonesmith in a green blur, fracturing his ribs with a sharp crack. As the chain coiled back into her hand, Shemira advanced, and the chain's seething resentment transformed into raging bloodlust, tearing the Bonesmith's body apart.
    "You've tortured us for too long!"
    "An eye for an eye! A tooth for a tooth!"
    "No mercy!"
    Countless voices rang out from within Shemira as she mindlessly unleashed her hatred, relentlessly lashing with the chain even as the Bonesmith lay motionless.

    Suddenly, Shemira felt something tugging behind her. She spun around, clawing viciously at the air.
    "Ma..."
    Her hand stopped mid-swing. Shemira slowly realized it was a young boy clutching her sleeve.
    She kneeled down and hugged Daimon as hard as she could.

174.Name: Ringer
174.Story:
Within the Heresy Inquisition of Greytide, the priests were embroiled in a heated debate. Priest Eismin, tired of the fruitless arguments, angrily rose from his seat. "Dura, pardon my utterance of this profane name, but the Chiming Order, Bantus' covert cult, is on the verge of infiltrating us. Both citizens and nobles have embraced the undead doctrine. If any doubts persist, this manuscript will bring clarity."
    With that, he slapped a worn page onto the table for all to see.
       <c><line></c>
    "Remember," my editor-in-chief cryptically advised when I first entered the trade, "tall branches have deep roots that delve into the depths." In those early days, I clung to his words like gospel, believing they'd lead me to fame and fortune. Now, after launching my own newspaper not long ago, I hunted for a major scoop for the inaugural issue.
    Lady Simona was the name whispered secretly among the upper crust of the city, and she was my target.
    Rumors suggested Lady Simona presented different personas to each, but her services were highly regarded. For nobles and tycoons facing issues that money and power couldn't solve, she was their last resort. I can confirm her ties to influential figures, some seemingly under her influence. She's rumored to be an illusionist, a poisoner, and even a noble's lover. Such secrets were regular gossip among the commoners. I thought exposing her and leaking a few scandals about the gentry would make our paper a sensation... How naive I was.
    On that fateful day, I disguised myself as a country baron. After persistent inquiries, I secured an audience with Lady Simona. Concealed behind veils and incense, her tall, slender form and cold elegance were evident. She spoke little but with a charming, antiquated accent. In our brief meeting, I spun a tale that a slovenly widower was disrupting my life. At the conclusion, Lady Simona simply said, "I'm willing to assist with your troubles." I responded with a knowing smile, confident she'd taken the bait. When I asked about payment, Lady Simona merely reached through the veil and revealed a small bell. She gently shook it, and an eerie chime resonated in my mind. When I regained my senses, she calmly instructed, "Place this bell in your home. Return it when my work is complete." I followed her directive, hanging the bell by my window, curious to see what tricks she had up her sleeve.
    On the third day, my partner in this endeavor, Daly the "widower," could not be reached. We had agreed to meet regularly to exchange information. The bell would ring unexpectedly, causing me to lose consciousness each time. Worried for Daly, I decided to check on him at night. At his residence, I found the door unlocked and the lights off. I called softly to him but received no answer. As I navigated to the study, a familiar ringing echoed in my mind. In the moonlight, I saw Daly lifeless at his desk, my name scrawled on parchment. Shocked, I collapsed. In my panic, I felt a presence behind me. Lady Simona, her pallid face visible, said, "Baron, your issue has been resolved." Fear overcame me, and I fled. I sought refuge in the countryside, but even miles from the bell, its eerie sound still haunted me. Each time it chimed, I couldn't help but dwell on Daly's fate and Lady Simona's haunting voice.
    After enduring countless nightmares, I had no choice.
    I returned to my dwelling, finding the bell undisturbed, swaying gently in the ocean breeze. As if compelled, I impulsively shook the bell as I removed it. The ringing filled the room, swirling and bouncing, escaping through the window only to return, infiltrating my thoughts once more. For the first time, I yearned for this painful experience. I couldn't resist ringing it a second and third time. That entire night, I remained spellbound by the bell's tolling, as if it kneaded my soul, making me savor death, the essence, and rebirth. It beckoned, whispering softly, 'Return... return.' In a haze, I brought the bell to Lady Simona's boudoir, where she remained behind the thin veil. The bell demanded my surrender, and I obediently handed it to her. The moment Lady Simona took it back, the ringing in my mind ceased abruptly, as if I had never heard it before, ripping away a part of my soul.
    "The contract is fulfilled, Baron, or should I say, Mr. Editor. You may leave now." Lady Simona said flatly.
    I had failed, paying a cruel price for my ambitions. There were depths to the darkness that exceeded my ability to withstand. All I can do now is record it all to warn those who come after.

    (A final line in the corner. Hastily scribbled in frantic handwriting.)
    I cannot escape that sound. I must return. 
     <c><line></c>
    "This editor's paper promotes the undead's doctrine. We seized this discarded manuscript from his residence, though he disclaims authorship. Our investigation of this Lady Simona has encountered secret resistance from the nobility. Thus, I propose submitting this matter for a vote and seeking aid from the Holy Tribunal in the capital," urged Priest Eismin.
    To Eismin's surprise, only a few of his fellow priests raised their hands. Just as he was about to speak again, a strange ringing suddenly resonated in his ears...

175.Name: BassD
175.Story:
One afternoon, a curiously dressed musician showed up at my door, hoping I would give my stamp of approval. His name was Lavatune, and he had made a name for himself in the small local taverns in Oakenfell. Now that he had a cult following, he wanted to make his presence known on a bigger stage.
 
     I turned down his request to perform on the spot for me because, to be honest, I wasn't interested in the type of music he played. As a well-known critic, all I had to do was scribble a few words, and I could make or break someone's career. It didn't matter if I'd never actually heard them perform before. My "impartial" reviews carried a lot of weight in these parts.
 
     To me, there was no sweeter melody than the clink of coins. Having a loyal following meant he had value I could exploit.
 
     With little fanfare, we signed a contract. My endorsement would bring him more fans, and he would have to do shows at my request. The contract seemed standard, but between all the dense clauses was the trap I had carefully designed for him. If he slipped up during a performance, he would owe me a ridiculous amount of money and be at my mercy for the rest of his life.
 
     "The poor kid has no idea what he's got himself into," I thought.
 
     Lavatune's first show was at a small concert hall I arranged for him. Before he took the stage, I had already planted my men in the audience. Their job was to cause a scene and have Lavatune screw up—just like I had done to countless other musicians. Meanwhile, I could just relax at home and wait for him to breach his contract. When he showed up crying and begging for mercy, I would make him my personal money-making tool like all the others.
 
     However, to my surprise, Lavatune's performance went off without a hitch. My men somehow forgot my orders and became among his followers. This made me uneasy. Things were getting out of my control.
 
     According to our deal, Lavatune would perform at a bigger venue soon. This time, I decided I would be there in person to see what kind of magic he had up his sleeve. The day of the show, I told my entourage to be ready. As soon as the music started, my men would mess up his performance. I kept the contract close at hand—the second he slipped up, I would declare his breach of contract and claim him as my own.
 
     Showtime approached. The lights dimmed, leaving Lavatune's sly expression faintly lit on stage. I could not wait to see the shock on his face.
 
     "Let the show begin!"
 
     Lavatune stood center stage, unleashing a heavy, resonating sound from a four-stringed instrument. I signaled my men to make their move, but they just stared blankly. All of a sudden, a bizarre fervor took hold, and they started convulsing uncontrollably.
 
     Lavatune began to play more intensely. Each note felt like a razor blade, piercing my eardrums and stabbing my soul. I watched the crowd get almost hypnotized by the music, swaying to the sounds.
 
     As the notes clashed and collided, the air began to smell like sulfur. Try as I may, I couldn't resist the surreal music, like invisible hands clawing at my soul.
 
     Lavatune's music grew frenzied and wild. The piercing strings sounded like wails from the netherworld. The audience's eyes flashed with madness, full of zeal and worship, fully converted to his cause. They chanted his name. The cacophony weaved with the music into some kind of freakish symphony.
 
     Suddenly, the music stopped, and the whole hall fell silent. Everyone's eyes turned to me, cold and emotionless. Lavatune stood center stage, a crazed glint in his eyes as if he could see right through me. His hair turned an eerie crimson, and gnarly horns twisted out from underneath.
 
     "Welcome, critic," Lavatune's voice boomed as if from the abyss itself. "You thought you were the master of this game, but in truth, you were just my pawn."
 
     I could not believe that the man I had signed a contract with was a real Hypogean! Dizzy and desperate, I tried to escape, but it was hopeless. Lavatune's music swelled again, even stronger than before. The crowd's eyes blazed with fervor as if beholding their deity.
 
     The jarring sounds made my body lose control as if invisible strings were being attached.
 
     "Do you wish to break our arrangement?" the Hypogean's whisper was followed by an evil laugh.
 
     I felt a searing heat in my chest. The contract in my hand burned to ash, but the words were etched into my flesh. There was no breaking free from the Hypogean's hold. The contract bound me to keep bringing him fresh souls until I died. However, I couldn't accept defeat. For someone like me who got off on controlling others, becoming a slave was a fate worse than death. With my final ounce of will, I tried to draw my dagger and aim it at my heart.
 
     In the end, Lavatune got what he wanted, and I will continue booking shows for him... forever.

210.Name: BloodS
210.Story:
Lord Ainz, my one and only, my beloved master...
    As the guardian of the first, second, and third floors, I bear the responsibility of safeguarding the Great Tomb of Nazarick, but what worries me even more right now is your own safety... Lord Peroroncino, my creator, bestowed me with great loyalty and love, and these feelings only grow stronger when I see you...

    You still refuse to speak to me, Lord Ainz. Are you still angry with me? Of course, after what happened... To this day, when I think back on it, I still feel a great burden of shame. At that time, I was afraid that you'd abandon me, as I'd been nothing more than a useless servant who'd only brought you trouble... While you did punish me tenderly, allowing my heart to regain peace over time... I'm still fearful that I'll never regain your trust after such unfaithful mistakes.
    Please believe me, Lord Ainz, your flawless figure is simply the pinnacle of beauty! To me, you are the greatest and most spectacular being in the universe! But how could you leave the Great Tomb of Nazarick all alone, without saying a single word...

    I can wait no longer. I must find you at once.

    Your servants are simply too worried about you. Fortunately, Sebas detected in your chambers a trace of a magical fluctuation that had not completely dissipated, and we managed to find a locator message in your logbook... Although... You only sent the message to Albedo?
    Do you know how fast my heart is beating now, Lord Ainz? My bosom is bursting with a blend of jealousy and endless anxiety! Could it be that the recently-vanished Albedo used teleportation magic with you?! Curses, you even told her your destination! I must've not done enough, since she's beat me to the chase... Whenever I imagine you enjoying time together with Albedo, my heart blazes with jealousy and rage... But that doesn't stop me from worshipping and adoring you!
    In any case, I will follow your every step. I will not hesitate, even if it means visiting an unknown world.

    I didn't waste a single moment, Lord Ainz. After finding your location, the glow of teleportation engulfed me... Oh, what an intense sensation that my whole body trembled! I was instantly teleported to a new and unfamiliar world... This place is so different from Nazarick, with its gorgeous scenery—but behind it all seems to lurk a strange threatening feeling...
    But despite that, it would all be worth it if I could lay eyes on you in this world! Don't mock my recklessness in coming here alone—your safety is my top priority! No matter what trials I might face, I won't let that old hag Albedo spend another minute with you!

    Lord Ainz, you must be waiting for me somewhere in this strange world... Right?
